name: _blocks
docstring:
Yield the response body in READ_BLOCK-sized pieces.

    `http.client.HTTPResponse.read(n)` is the real path here, and the sized read
    is the whole point: `for raw in resp` reads until a newline, so a body that
    never sends one is already a single unbounded `bytes` by the time the caller
    is handed it. Some response-like objects only support iteration (a test
    stand-in, a pre-split body); those keep their own framing, and the byte
    ceiling in `_BoundedLines` still applies to what they yield.

name: _BoundedLines
docstring:
Newline framing over a response body, with a hard byte ceiling.

    Three unbounded reads close here. The body arrives in fixed blocks, so no
    single newline-less line can grow without limit; the running total stops the
    stream once `limit` bytes have been taken, so a trickle of well-formed small
    deltas cannot either; and `deadline` stops it once the whole transfer has
    run longer than a real answer ever does, which is the case neither of the
    other two catches -- a host sending one byte at a time, slowly, stays under
    the byte ceiling forever and resets the socket timeout

name: _note_truncated
docstring:
Say on stderr that the answer was cut off at the byte ceiling.

    A ceiling that silently drops the tail turns a partial answer into one that
    looks whole, which is the failure mode `_empty_answer` exists to avoid for
    the no-text case. stderr, not stdout, for the same reason `_disclose` uses
    it: stdout is the answer and has to stay pipeable.

name: _note_timed_out
docstring:
Say on stderr that the stream ran past its wall-clock budget.

    Distinct wording from `_note_truncated` on purpose: "too slow" and "too
    much" point at different causes, and a user who sees the byte-ceiling
    message for a stalled endpoint will go looking for an answer that was never
    large.

name: _writer
docstring:
A write callable that cannot raise UnicodeEncodeError.

    Always writes through the stream's own text-mode `write`, never through
    `sys.stdout.buffer`: on Windows the console expects bytes in its active
    codepage (cp1252, cp437, ...), and writing raw UTF-8 bytes straight to
    the buffer bypasses `TextIOWrapper`'s console translation, producing
    mojibake even though no exception is raised (#169). A non-ASCII token
    from a model would otherwise abort the whole answer mid-sentence, so the
    chunk is folded to what the stream's own encoding can represent first.

    whether the app is about to be exposed: pass the host you are going to bind,
    and loopback stays silent because loopback with no token is the documented

docstring:

    Two things do the work. Every frame is quantized against a single palette
    taken from the last (busiest) frame, so consecutive frames share colour
    indices and GIF's own delta coding can fire -- a per-frame adaptive palette
    re-encodes the whole canvas each time and roughly triples the file. And
    runs of identical frames (the typing pause, the hold at the end) collapse
    into one frame with a longer delay instead of dozens of copies.

Skipping an alias as a seed must leave it available to expansion.

    This is the half that makes D7 worth anything: the alias is how a caller of
    the public name reaches the private implementation, and it arrives as a
    graph neighbour. Marking it seen in the seed loop would silently delete
    that path, and the retrieval benchmark would lose the point it just gained.

    An alias is *nothing but* a name, so it collects `NAME_TERM_BOOST` more
    reliably than any real definition can: here its name is literally the
    query's strongest term. The seed loop skips aliases, so a boosted alias
    cannot reach a pack -- but the re-rank window is `k * 3`, and an alias
    hauled up it pushes a real candidate out. That is the one way an alias can
    still cost an answer after being made unseedable.

    whole body became one `bytes` object regardless of its size. Here the body
    is a single valid JSON object a full megabyte past the ceiling -- more than
    the one-block overshoot the bound allows, so an unbounded read cannot slip
    under it -- and carries no newline anywhere.

name: test_a_trickling_provider_cannot_stream_forever
docstring:
Axis 3 (C26b): a slow stream is bounded by wall-clock time, not bytes.

    Neither existing bound closes this. `MAX_ANSWER_BYTES` only fires once the
    body is enormous, and this one is a few kilobytes. `HTTP_TIMEOUT` measures
    the gap *between* reads and resets whenever a byte arrives, so a host that
    sends a little, forever, never trips it. Before `MAX_ANSWER_SECONDS` the
    call had no upper bound on its own duration at all.

    The budget is the real `MAX_ANSWER_SECONDS`, not a shrunken one, so a
    fixture that is merely short cannot pass this by accident.

    Without the re-rank the class header outscores the method that answers the

    to match many of them. With the re-rank the order inverts, so under a

    boost more reliably than the implementation does.

    `test_middleware_chaining_runs_handlers_in_order` overlaps "how are
    middleware handlers chained together" on two terms and would take the full
    boost; `compose_middleware`, which is the answer, overlaps on one and takes
    half. Boosting by name and demoting by path then fight, and the boost wins
    (2.0 * TEST_SEED_PENALTY = 1.2 still beats an unboosted source chunk), which
    reintroduces exactly the defect `TEST_SEED_PENALTY` exists to remove.

    also eligible for the boost.

    Sparing a chunk the penalty and then denying it the boost is not protection
    -- it leaves it to lose its slot to every sibling that can collect 1.5x.
    That is what dropped `app/store.py` from the demo's "trace an order request
    from route to persistence", the one starter question whose answer spans four
    modules, while `CONTAINER_PENALTY_MIN_TOKENS` was doing its job.

    U+DC80-U+DCFF fine and raises `UnicodeEncodeError` on everything else in the

name: _require_working_cpp

    `shutil.which("cpp") is not None` is not that condition and was the reason

    -- can each fail or time out on a loaded runner. Both failures are
    swallowed into `used_cpp=False`, so the assertion below reported "cpp citation accuracy
    regressed" for an environment that simply could not prep

name: test_cpp_fallback_line_numbers_match_original
docstring: Verify used_cpp=True must still cite the on-disk file, not cpp -P rows.

name: _cpp_calls

name: test_the_cpp_version_probe_runs_once_across_many_erroring_files
docstring:
#239: `cpp --version` answers the same thing for the life of the
    process, so a macro-heavy tree must not pay a second spawn per file. The
    count asserted is a hand-derived literal -- one probe, one preprocess per
    file -- not a number the parser computed.

name: test_a_failed_probe_is_retried_rather_than_cached
docstring:
#239: only a *successful* probe is memoized, exactly as
    fetch._git_version does it. A transient fd-exhaustion or fork failure must
    not disable the cpp fallback for the rest of the process's life -- which is
    precisely what functools.lru_cache would do here.

name: test_both_cpp_invocations_close_stdin
docstring:
#240: capture_output redirects the child's stdout and stderr only, so
    without stdin=DEVNULL cpp inherits ours -- under repo2graph-mcp on stdio
    that handle is the client's JSON-RPC pipe. Asserted at the call site as
    well as in test_compat's whole-package AST sweep.

name: test_cpp_retry_never_names_the_file_or_follows_includes
docstring:
#475: cpp resolves #include, so an untrusted file could point it at
    /dev/zero or any readable path. The retry feeds the source on stdin with
    every file-opening directive blanked, in all the spellings cpp accepts.

name: test_run_cpp_stops_a_macro_bomb_at_the_limit
docstring:
#456 P4: 40 doubling macros expand to ~2^40 tokens. capture_output held
    all of it in this process before the size check ran; the stream stops one
    byte past the limit and kills cpp.

name: test_the_cpp_child_is_refused_memory_past_its_cap
docstring:
The bomb above is stopped for its *output*; this is about what cpp spent
    getting there, which nothing bounded.

    cpp allocates while expanding and before it prints, so the output bound
    cannot see it. The same 40-deep doubling bomb drove `cc1` to **32.6 GB** on
    a CI runner whose commit limit is 33.6 GB -- which never failed a parse. It
    failed whatever else on the machine asked for memory next, surfacing as
    unrelated tests dying with `MemoryError`, `WinError 1455` and
    `RuntimeError: can't start new thread`, on a different test each run.

    Driven with a Python child

name: test_run_cpp_asks_for_the_memory_cap
docstring:
Platform-independent half: whatever the OS does with it, `_run_cpp` must
    request the cap for the pid it just spawned. A refactor that drops the call
    puts the 32.6 GB back.

name: test_include_strip_is_linear_on_nested_comment_lookalikes
docstring:
CodeQL py/redos: `/\\*.*?\\*/` inside a repeated group backtracked
    exponentially on `#/*` followed by many `*//*`.

    CPU time, not wall clock, for the reason `test_secrets_hardening.py`'s
    three linearity checks give: under `-n auto` on a shared runner,
    preemption alone can stretch this work past a one-second wall bound, which
    turns a ReDoS detector into a test of how busy the machine is. The fixed
    form costs ~0.02 s of CPU here, so the bound keeps its 50x margin while
    the backtracking form takes seconds.

name: demo_index

name: test_every_fixture_module_carries_a_file_chunk
docstring:
chunks.py drops a `file_residual` under 40 chars, and a node with no
    chunk can be neither a seed nor a retrievable neighbour.

    Verified as a detector against a module with no module-level text at all
    (`def a(): return 1`), which is the condition that actually trips the
    40-char floor -- a module keeping only its imports stays above it. So the
    thing this guards is a fixture module stripped of its docstring *and* its
    module-level constant, which is exactly how the residue rule gets broken
    by someone tidying up.

    See CONTRIBUTING.md, "A file with little residue emit

name: test_demo_graph_has_the_edges_the_starter_questions_rely_on

Hand-derived from the fixture source: routes guard -> service -> store.

name: test_demo_has_no_cross_language_call_edges
docstring:
The JS client must not resolve into the Python store.

    `web/client.js` calls the browser global `fetch()`; when the Python store
    had a method of the same name, the global-name fallback produced a
    `web/client.js::createOrder -> app/store.py::OrderStore.fetch` edge. That
    is a real property of the resolver, but a first-run demo is the wrong
    place to display one -- the fixture is named to avoid the collision, and
    this pins it so a future rename cannot quietly bring it back.

name: test_each_starter_question_cites_the_file_that_answers_it

The quickstart promises these five prompts work. This is that promise.

name: test_bare_repo2graph_lists_every_subcommand
docstring:
`repo2graph` with no arguments is the first thing a new user types.

    so that help page listed no commands at all -- "positional arguments: {}"
    -- while `repo2graph --help` listed all of them. Asserting on `demo` and
    `build` alone would not have caught it either, since both are absent from
    the broken page *and* the empty one; what pins it is that the two pages
    agree.

name: sample_repo
docstring:
A tree with enough shape that ordering has something to get wrong:
    several directories, several languages, cross-file calls and imports.

name: test_two_builds_of_one_tree_are_byte_identical
docstring: The baseline property: build twice, same bytes.

name: test_serial_and_parallel_builds_agree
docstring:
`--jobs N` must not reorder anything.

    `parse_all` uses `pool.map`, which preserves input order, and the build
    loop consumes results in discovery order -- but the fixture is far under
    PARALLEL_MIN_FILES, so the pool never starts for it. Drop the threshold so
    the parallel path is the one actually exercised here.

name: _reversed_walk
docstring:
os.walk with every directory listing reversed.

    This stands in for "the same tree on a different filesystem". A
    same-machine A/B cannot see an enumeration-order bug at all: NTFS returns
    entries alphabetically, so the unsorted order and the sorted order happen
    to coincide, and every assertion passes while the bug is live. ext4 with
    dir_index returns hash order, which does not coincide.

name: test_filesystem_enumeration_order_does_not_change_the_index
docstring:
The bug this suite exists for.

    Discovery order *is* artifact order. `git ls-files` sorts its output but
    `os.walk` does not, so the same tree indexed on two machines produced
    three artifacts that differed byte-for-byte while describing an identical
    graph.

name: test_git_and_walk_discovery_agree_on_the_same_tree
docstring:
A tree with nothing ignored must index identically with and without git.

    Same content, two discovery sources: `git ls-files` when `.git` is
    present, `os.walk` when it is not. They are only interchangeable if both
    are sorted, which is the invariant `discover()` now enforces in one place
    for both branches.

name: test_incremental_rebuild_equals_a_full_rebuild
docstring:
`--incremental` is a speed optimisation, not a different index.

    A reused `ParsedFile` is exact -- it is a pure function of the file's
    bytes and language -- and everything downstream (the global name index,
    CALLS confidences, INHERITS, entrypoints, reach) is recomputed from the
    full symbol set regardless. So the output must be byte-identical, not
    merely close, both when nothing changed and after an edit.

name: test_manifest_is_identical_apart_from_the_two_provenance_fields
docstring:
Everything in manifest.json is reproducible except build_id and created_at.

    Pinned as an explicit allowlist rather than "ignore whatever differs", so
    a third non-deterministic field added later fails here instead of quietly
    joining the exceptions.

name: test_max_files_truncation_is_deterministic
docstring:
`--max-files N` takes the first N in discovery order.

    Unsorted discovery made this actively dangerous rather than merely
    untidy: which files landed in a truncated index depended on the
    filesystem, so two machines indexed *different subsets* of the same tree
    and each answered questions the other could not. The reversed walk is
    what makes this a detector -- under the real one, NTFS order and sorted
    order coincide and the assertion holds either way.

name: test_every_exclusion_glob_matches_its_representative_paths
docstring:
A pattern that matches nothing is worse than no pattern.

    `parse._glob_re` anchors a pattern containing "/" at the repository root,
    so `vendor/**` silently misses `packages/web/vendor/...` -- which is
    where a monorepo keeps all of it. Each group declares the paths it must
    cover; this runs them through the real matcher.

name: test_exclusion_groups_do_not_match_ordinary_source

`explain-path` must answer from the rule set the build would use.

    It also has to name *which* pattern matched: a `--exclude-group` expands
    to as many as 60 globs, and echoing the whole list buries the answer in

name: test_explain_path_takes_builds_path_flags

name: test_discovery_sort_key_is_posix

Sorting on str(Path) would sort on "\\" on Windows and "/" elsewhere --

name: test_explain_path_knows_discover_never_indexes_an_index

`explain-path .r2g/agent/nodes.jsonl` said INCLUDED; no build indexes it.

name: test_languages_documented
docstring:
Verify every LANG_CFG grammar key is documented in README.md.

    Word-boundary regexes, not plain substrings: `"c" in readme_text.lower()`
    or `"go" in ...` is true of nearly any English prose regardless of
    whether the language is mentioned, so those checks passed even with the
    language name deleted from README.md. `\\bC\\b` (with a negative
    lookahead so it doesn't also match the "C" inside "C++"/"C#") actually
    requires the token to appear.

name: test_language_scorecard_matches_the_generator
docstring:
The scorecard table in docs/architecture.md is what the generator emits today.

    `scripts/generate_language_scorecard.py` shipped with no consumer: nothing in
    docs/, README or CI referenced it, and its own docstring pointed at a
    `docs/LANGUAGE_SCORECARD.json` that was never committed. A generator whose
    output nobody reads stops being run, and then stops being right -- it scores
    `LANG_CFG` by introspection, so every language added or extended moves these
    numbers silently.

    Pinning the rendered table means adding a language fails here until the table
    is regenerated

The five starter prompts are authored once, in repo2graph/demo.py.

    README.md renders them and `repo2graph demo` runs them, so a prompt edited

name: test_expansion_trace_follows_the_same_directions_retrieve_does
docstring:
`expand()` defaults to DEFAULT_EDGE_DIRS, which is DEFINES-`in` only, but
    `retrieve()` passes ALL_EDGE_DIRS. An explain that takes the default traces
    a walk the retrieval below it never made -- it reported
    `Runner.run -> Runner DEFINES in` while the chunk it printed came back
    labelled `DEFINES out of main.py`.

    The tuple below is hand-derived from the fixture source: `Runner` defines
    the method `run`, so `sym:main.py::Runner` has a DEFINES edge *out* to
    `sym:main.py::Runner.run`. Set membership only -- no rank, score or
    order.

name: test_every_retrieved_neighbour_appears_in_the_expansion_trace
docstring:

    show. This is the property the direction filter broke, stated without
    naming any one edge.

    The query is "modes" and not the three-term one above on purpose: it seeds
    on `file:main.py` alone, so both of the fixture's neighbours really are
    expanded rather than seeded, and the narrowed `DEFINES: ("in",)` leaves one
    of them retrieved but untraced. With a query that seeds every node the
    branch is vacuous.

name: test_legend_and_manifest_describe_types_identically

    same type, because they now read from the one definition.

    Detector proof: before this fix, viz.py's NODE_TYPE_DESC/EDGE_TYPE_DESC
    used shorter, independently-worded copy (e.g. "the repository itself"
    vs. export.py's "the repository itself; one per index") -- this

    `_fit` reads 0 as "no ceiling", which is the caller's sentinel; it was also
    what `budget - len(header)` came to once the header outgrew the budget, so
    every merged chunk came back. Measured at 25x the stated ceiling, with
    `truncated` reporting False.

    is why `_fit` takes None rather than reading 0 two ways.

0.x bundles every grammar in the wheel; 1.x downloads them on first use.

    0.13.0 ships a 33 MB wheel. 1.20.0 ships 2.5 MB and an 89 KB sdist, fetching

    user's source. That contradicts the no-network guarantee in README.md and
    .github/SECURITY.md, and makes `uv.lock` and the SBOM describe a loader
    rather than what actually executes. A dependabot bump must not quietly undo
    this, so the bound is asserted rather than merely commented.

    So slice 1 (bytes 0.._LIMIT) ends on the lone lead byte 0xC3 and slice 2

    to decode and both were dropped, taking alpha and beta with the first and
    gamma with the second.

    A 0.5 confidence floor severed the walk at the ambiguous hop and returned
    `affected_tests: []` -- a silent false negative, which in CI means a green
    run over code nothing exercised.

    The point is that the trade is reported rather than implicit: the same walk
    that loses the test also sets `truncated`, so a CI caller can tell a
    provably complete subset from a lossy one.

name: test_affected_tests_sees_through_a_test_helper
docstring:
A test reached only via a fixture/helper module must not be dropped.

    `is_test_path` is true of every module under `tests/` -- `conftest.py`,
    fixtures, assertion helpers -- and `derived.py` seeds a `TESTS` edge from
    the helper nearest the modified code. The walk used to mark that helper
    visited without ever expanding it, so the real `test_*.py` callers one hop
    further out were never reached, and the frontier still drained, so nothing
    reported the answer as incomplete. Fixtures and helpers are the common case,
    which made this the same silent false negative in a new p

name: test_affected_tests_does_not_follow_a_shadowed_builtin
docstring:
Editing a function that shadows a builtin must not select the whole suite.

    A `shadowed_builtin` edge is not an ambiguous *candidate* the way a 1/n
    name-resolution edge is -- the call almost certainly went to the builtin and
    the user symbol merely shares its name. Following them turned a two-line
    edit into "run every test that calls `len()`", which is the feature failing
    in the over-selection direction.

name: test_affected_tests_admits_it_cannot_see_fixture_injection
docstring:
Reaching a conftest means the untraceable consumers must be declared.

    A test that *receives* a pytest fixture never calls it by name, so there is
    no call edge and the consumer is invisible to the walk. Here 30 tests reach
    the modified function only that way: the selection is `['tests/conftest.py']`
    and the frontier drains, so without this guard the answer would be reported
    as complete while missing every test that actually exercises the change.

name: test_affected_tests_stays_complete_without_a_conftest
docstring:
The fixture caveat must not fire on a repo that has no conftest in range.

    `truncated` is only useful if it means something, so the guard is
    conditioned on actually reaching a conftest rather than on the repository
    containing fixtures anywhere.

name: test_follow_shadowed_builtins_recovers_the_dropped_edges
docstring:
The shadowed-builtin exclusion is a heuristic, so it must be overridable.

    Dropping those edges is right by default -- the call almost always went to
    the builtin -- but a codebase that really does define and call its own `len`
    would otherwise have no way to select the tests that exercise it, and no way
    to correct a heuristic that is wrong about their code.

name: _ParserReached
docstring: Sentinel raised in place of `parse_args`, to stop an entrypoint at its parser.

name: _registered_options
docstring:
Every option string the entrypoint's parser and its subparsers accept.

    An exit status alone is not a sufficient check here and a first draft of
    this file was fooled by exactly that: a re-added `--http-port` that takes a
    value still makes `main(["--http-port"])` exit 2, because argparse now
    complains that the argument is missing rather than that the option is
    unknown. Reading the registered options instead asks the question directly
    -- is this flag back? -- and cannot be satisfied by a different error.

    The parser is built inside `main`, so it is captured by standin

name: _imported_modules
docstring:
Every module name `path` actually imports, from its AST.

    Over `ast.Import` / `ast.ImportFrom` rather than a substring scan, because
    `answer.py` and `security.py` both contain "http" and "jwt" in contexts that
    have nothing to do with importing one: URL handling in the former, and a
    literal list of secret-bearing key names in the latter (`security.py` has
    `"jwt"` as a credential pattern). A grep for those words over the package
    reports both files and tells you nothing.

    Relative imports are skipped -- `from .auth import ...` cannot name a
    third-party library, and

name: test_auth_and_http_server_modules_are_gone_from_disk
docstring:
The two deleted files must not come back under their old names.

    A restored `auth.py` or `http_server.py` would be dead code at best -- no
    caller is left -- and at worst an unreviewed resurrection of the crypto the
    removal existed to delete. Checked on disk as well as through the import
    system so that a file present but never imported still fails.

name: test_removed_modules_are_not_importable
docstring:
`import repo2graph.auth` must still fail.

    Separate from the on-disk check: a module can be re-introduced as a package
    directory, or re-exported from somewhere else under the old name, and either
    would make the import succeed while no `auth.py` file exists.

name: test_mcp_entrypoint_registers_no_removed_flag
docstring:
`repo2graph-mcp` must not have any of the ten flags back on its parser.

    This is the regression that matters most, and the one an exit status alone
    cannot see. A config left over from 2.2.0 says `--auth-token hunter2`; if
    the parser ever accepts it again -- even as a deprecated no-op -- the user
    is told the server started and is never told their bearer token guards
    nothing. stdio inherits the parent process's identity, so there is no
    meaning left to give any of these.

name: test_cli_registers_no_removed_flag
docstring:
Nor may the `repo2graph` CLI, on any of its subcommands.

    The CLI never served MCP over HTTP, but it is the binary users reach for
    first and the obvious place to retry a flag that `repo2graph-mcp` just
    refused. Checked across every subparser rather than at top level only,
    because `build` and `github` are where a plausible-looking `--auth-token`
    would be added.

name: test_mcp_entrypoint_exits_nonzero_on_a_removed_flag
docstring:
Passing a removed flag must fail the process, not be quietly dropped.

    The companion to the registration check: that one proves the option is not
    declared, this one proves the end-to-end behaviour a 2.2.0 user actually
    hits. Exit 2 is argparse's own code for an unrecognised argument, so the
    status is asserted rather than the wording, which argparse is free to
    reword between Python versions. `serve` is stubbed so that an accepted flag
    shows up as a recorded call instead of a server blocking on stdin forever.

name: test_cli_exits_nonzero_on_a_removed_flag
docstring: The CLI fails the same way, so neither binary silently accepts one.

name: test_no_module_imports_an_http_framework_or_jwt_library
docstring:
No file under `repo2graph/` may import a web framework or a JWT library.

    The flag checks above only cover the two parsers. This covers the shape of
    the regression that does not go through a flag at all: a new module that
    imports `fastapi` or `jwt` and brings the transport back beside the stdio
    server rather than in place of it. It also keeps the README's and
    SECURITY.md's "no network calls" claim honest at the dependency level.

name: write_repo
docstring: Materialise `files` (default FILES) under `root/src`; returns the dir.

name: build
docstring: Run the CLI build, returning its parsed JSON report.

name: artifact
docstring: Read one artifact's bytes, for byte-identity comparisons.

name: snapshot
docstring: Every artifact that describes the graph, as raw bytes.

name: RecordingParser
docstring: Wraps `parse_source` and records which languages/bodies it parsed.

name: test_unchanged_files_are_not_reparsed
docstring: The whole point: a second incremental build parses nothing at all.

name: test_added_file_is_the_only_one_parsed
docstring: Adding a file re-parses that file and nothing else.

name: _run_capture
docstring: Run an incremental build and return the CLI's JSON report text.

name: test_modified_file_is_reparsed
docstring: Editing one file re-parses exactly that file.

name: _calls_edges
docstring: {(src, dst): confidence} for every CALLS edge in the index.

name: test_adding_a_duplicate_name_elsewhere_lowers_confidence_repo_wide
docstring:
The cross-file case the BACKLOG named as the blocker.

    `caller.entry` calls `handle`. With one `handle` in the repo the edge is
    confidence 1.0. Adding a *second* `handle` in a file the caller never
    imports must drop that edge to 0.5 and add a second candidate edge -- even
    though `pkg/caller.py` itself did not change and is served from cache.

name: test_deleting_a_file_removes_its_nodes_and_restores_confidence
docstring: Deleting a symbol's file removes its nodes and re-raises confidences.

name: test_renaming_a_symbol_updates_cross_file_calls
docstring: Renaming a callee in a changed file rewires the unchanged caller's edge.

name: test_entrypoint_flags_are_recomputed_not_spliced
docstring: A newly added caller must clear the callee's stale entrypoint flag.

name: test_incremental_is_byte_identical_to_a_full_rebuild
docstring:
The acceptance test: same bytes out, whatever route got there.

    Two checkouts of the same content, mutated identically. One is built fresh;
    the other is built once, mutated, then rebuilt incrementally. Every artifact
    must match byte for byte -- including `stats.json`, which is why the
    cached/re-parsed tallies live on `Graph.incremental` and not in `stats`.

name: test_incremental_against_a_repo_with_no_index_is_a_full_build
docstring: `--incremental` on a cold directory works; it simply has nothing to reuse.

name: test_a_corrupt_cache_falls_back_to_a_full_build
docstring: Garbage in `parse.cache.json` must cost a re-parse, never an exception.

name: test_a_future_cache_format_is_ignored
docstring: A cache from a newer repo2graph is dropped rather than half-read.

name: test_a_grammar_upgrade_invalidates_the_cache
docstring:
A tree-sitter upgrade must force a full re-parse, not a silent mix.

    `PARSE_CACHE_FORMAT` is bumped by hand and so only ever catches changes to
    *our* extraction. A grammar upgrade changes what the same bytes parse to
    while nothing in this repository changes, so the format constant stays put
    and `--incremental` would reuse every entry for every unmodified file. The
    index would then be half old-grammar and half new, and
    `test_incremental_is_byte_identical_to_a_full_rebuild` cannot see it because
    it never changes grammars mid-run.

name: test_a_cache_written_before_grammars_were_keyed_is_ignored
docstring:
Entries from an older repo2graph carry no `grammars` key.

    They were produced by a grammar version that was never recorded, so there is
    no way to tell whether they are reproducible. Absent must read as a miss,
    not as "no constraint".

name: test_same_bytes_different_language_is_a_cache_miss
docstring:
A rename that changes the language must not reuse the old parse.

    `a.py` and `a.rs` can hold byte-identical content and parse to completely
    different symbol sets, so the content hash alone is not a sufficient key.

name: entry_calls
docstring: The `(src, dst, type, resolution_kind)` tuples `entry` emits on disk.

name: test_incremental_preserves_import_alias_resolution
docstring:
An aliased import resolves identically on a cached rebuild.

    `import_details` was not persisted in the parse cache, so a cache hit lost
    every alias and the full build's `import_alias` edge came back as
    `CALLS_EXTERNAL` / `unresolved_external`.

    The module's headline byte-equality test cannot see this: a *plain*
    `from x import y` still resolves through the IMPORTS edges, which are
    rebuilt from `pf.imports`, and only the alias branch reads `import_details`.

name: test_incremental_rename_and_delete_sequence
docstring: End-to-end sequence: build -> rename -> incremental -> delete -> incremental -> modify -> compare.

name: test_a_changed_parse_option_invalidates_the_cache_and_says_why
docstring:
#302: cached entries depend on --max-file-mb and --chunk-large-files
    (whether a file was chunked) as much as on its bytes. Changing either must
    force a re-parse, and the build must say which key component changed.

name: test_a_first_incremental_build_reports_no_discarded_cache
docstring: No index yet is not a foreign index: there is no cache to discard.

name: test_a_language_table_edit_invalidates_the_cache
docstring:
#302: editing LANG_CFG changes every extraction without touching the
    grammars or PARSE_CACHE_FORMAT.

name: built
docstring: A small repository with an index built over it.

name: _git_init
docstring:
Make `src` a git checkout, with `.r2g/` ignored as a real repo would.

    Without the .gitignore, `git add -A` commits the index's own artifacts:
    `git ls-files` then returns them, the build indexes itself, and the tree
    reads as permanently dirty. That is a fixture artefact, not a behaviour
    worth asserting on -- README.md tells users to ignore `.r2g/`.

name: test_report_carries_every_promised_field
docstring: docs/architecture.md promises nine things. This is that list.

name: test_report_sections_are_the_documented_six
docstring:
The `--json` report is a public surface: `--json` prints it verbatim.

    Asserted against a real report rather than by scraping the source, so a
    section that is built but empty, or renamed in one place only, fails here.

name: test_symbol_and_edge_breakdowns_match_the_totals
docstring: The by-kind maps are a decomposition, not a second measurement.

name: test_freshness_detects_a_modified_file
docstring: mtime only chooses what to hash; the finding is a hash mismatch.

name: test_freshness_ignores_a_touched_but_unchanged_file
docstring:
A fresh clone rewrites every mtime without changing a byte. Calling
    that stale would make the check useless on exactly the machine -- CI --
    that most needs it.

name: test_freshness_does_not_count_the_index_as_added_source
docstring:
`.r2g` is not in DEFAULT_SKIP_DIRS and did not exist when the build ran
    discovery, so on a non-git tree every artifact it just wrote came back as
    a newly "added" source file and a brand-new index read as stale.

name: test_a_filtered_build_is_not_instantly_stale
docstring:
Freshness must re-discover with the filters the *build* used.

    Comparing against default filters re-finds every file the build
    deliberately excluded, reports them all as newly added, and so any build
    with `--exclude` or `--exclude-group` reads as stale the instant it
    finishes -- which makes the whole freshness signal worthless for exactly
    the users who configured indexing most carefully.

name: test_state_file_records_the_discovery_filters
docstring:
The filters are persisted, not re-derived -- there is nowhere else to
    recover `--exclude-group generated` from after the build exits.

name: test_freshness_falls_back_when_the_state_file_predates_filters
docstring:
An index built before filters were recorded must still be checkable,
    and must say that its comparison used defaults.

name: test_freshness_without_state_file_is_unknown_not_stale
docstring:
An index built by an older version cannot be checked at file level.
    "I could not tell" is not the same claim as "it is out of date".

name: test_freshness_respects_the_scan_bound
docstring:
Past the bound the file-level check is skipped and says so, rather
    than re-hashing an attacker-chosen number of bytes.

name: test_index_status_is_the_only_staleness_implementation
docstring:
Two implementations of "is this stale" drift until they contradict each
    other in front of a user. `index-status` owns the answer; `doctor` must not
    grow a second one, so this pins both halves: index-status still detects a
    stale tree, and doctor reports no freshness check at all.

name: test_repo2graphs_own_scratch_files_do_not_mark_the_tree_dirty
docstring:
A clean checkout must not record `dirty: true` because of repo2graph.

    `BuildLock` writes `..r2g.r2glock` and `dump_all` stages artifacts in
    `..r2g.staging.<pid>.<hex>/`, both *beside* the output directory so they
    survive the transactional swap -- which means `.r2g/` in .gitignore
    covers neither. Provenance is captured from inside both windows, so every
    build of a pristine repository used to report a dirty tree and blame the
    user for repo2graph's own scratch files.

name: test_cli_json_output_is_the_report_verbatim
docstring:
`index_status`'s docstring promises `--json` prints the report verbatim,
    so every key it returns is public API. That is the contract under test here:
    a full dict comparison, not a spot-check of a few keys, because a CLI that
    renamed or dropped one key on the way to stdout would break a consumer while
    still satisfying any subset assertion.

    `index.age_seconds` is the one legitimately volatile field -- whole seconds
    since the manifest was written -- so it is dropped from *both* sides rather
    than used as an excuse to weaken the comparison. Its presence is still
    ass

name: test_cli_check_flag_gates_on_freshness
docstring:
`--check` is the CI gate: a committed index that no longer matches the
    commit it claims is a reviewable failure, not a warning nobody reads.

name: test_pointing_at_the_agent_dir_gives_the_same_answer
docstring:
`doctor` documents accepting either the -o directory or `agent/`, and a
    caller who already resolved the path must not get a different report.

    The source tree is the *index root's* parent -- one level up from `.r2g`,
    two from `.r2g/agent` -- so deriving it from whatever directory was handed
    in pointed the freshness check at `.r2g` and reported every source file as
    removed.

name: test_malformed_state_json_handled_gracefully
docstring: Corrupted index.state.json reports stale gracefully without crashing.

name: test_cli_accepts_an_explicit_repo_path
docstring: The index need not live inside the tree it describes.

name: test_shipped_manifest_carries_no_absolute_source_root
docstring:
manifest.json ships (committed .r2g, Action artifacts): no build path in it.

    The absolute root lives in the index root's local.json, which a generated
    .gitignore keeps out of git, and index-status still finds it through there
    for an index built outside the tree it describes.

name: test_old_manifest_source_root_is_still_honoured
docstring: An index from before local.json existed keeps working.

name: test_github_build_is_reported_as_remote_not_stale
docstring:
`repo2graph github owner/repo -o dir`: the temp clone is gone afterwards.

    Comparing against cwd read as `[STALE] N added` and suggested `build <cwd>`,
    which indexes the wrong tree. It must say freshness cannot be checked and
    suggest the github command instead.

name: fake_clone
signature: def fake_clone(spec, workdir, ref=None, depth=0, token=None):

name: test_action_never_ships_local_json
docstring: The Action's upload and branch push both drop the machine-local file.

name: test_the_reported_path_lists_are_capped_but_the_counts_are_not
docstring:
`index-status --json` is a public surface, and a 4,000-entry list is not
    a report. The lists are capped at MAX_LISTED_PATHS; the counts beside them
    stay exact, which is what tells a reader the list was cut.

name: build_index
signature: def build_index(repo: Path, out: Path, extra_args=()) -> int:

name: test_ok_for_an_existing_index_dir
docstring:
An `agent/` subdirectory is what marks a directory as ours to reuse.

        That, and not the directory's name, is the recognition signal -- the
        contrast is `test_rejects_foreign_dir` below, which is the same call
        against a directory holding an unrelated file. A duplicate of this test
        asserted the same thing under the name
        `test_allows_dir_with_r2g_marker`, differing only in calling the
        directory `idx` instead of `.r2g`; `validate_outdir` never looks at the
        name, so it was the same case twice.

name: test_context_manager_holds_the_lock_then_releases_it
docstring:
The lock file exists for the duration of the block and not after.

        The previous assertion was `lock_file.exists() or True`, which is True
        whatever the lock does. The file is a *sibling* of the target, not a
        child -- `.idx.r2glock` next to `idx/` -- which is what that dead
        assertion was reaching for.

name: test_timeout_when_already_held
docstring: A second lock acquire on the same outdir must time out cleanly.

name: test_a_read_only_parent_fails_fast_instead_of_waiting_out_the_timeout
docstring:
EROFS cannot clear by itself, so retrying for the whole timeout and
        then blaming a holder that does not exist sends the user elsewhere.

name: test_a_windows_sharing_violation_is_retried_not_treated_as_unwritable
docstring:
OneDrive, antivirus and the search indexer briefly hold a new index's
        files open; NTFS answers EACCES until they let go, and it clears.

        `export._rename` already retries exactly that. This lock used to retry
        every OSError too, then started fast-failing on EACCES -- turning a
        self-clearing hiccup into a build failure that blamed a read-only
        parent. The third attempt here succeeds, so acquire() must as well.

name: test_stale_lock_is_reclaimed
docstring: A lock file from a non-existent PID is reclaimed on next acquire.

name: test_an_aged_lock_is_not_stolen_from_a_live_holder
docstring:
A build slower than the stale threshold keeps its lock.

        `_write_metadata` runs once, at acquire, so mtime measures how long
        the holder has been working -- not whether it is stuck. Reclaiming on
        that alone meant any build over the threshold was joined by a second.

name: test_releasing_does_not_unlink_a_lock_file_that_is_not_ours
docstring:
release() must not delete whatever happens to sit at the path.

        If the name was replaced while we held our file, the thing at the path
        is another holder's live lock; removing it would admit a third builder.

name: _index_naming
docstring: An index whose manifest declares one checksum, for `key`.

name: test_manifest_cannot_name_a_path_outside_the_index
docstring:
An absolute or escaping key must be refused before anything is read.

        `out / rel_path` discards `out` when rel_path is absolute, so the loop
        used to hash any file the process could reach and put the real digest
        in `errors` -- a hash-disclosure oracle -- while a missing file
        reported differently from a mismatching one, probing for existence.

name: test_a_relative_manifest_key_is_still_checked
docstring:
The guard must reject escapes only -- an ordinary key still verifies.

        Without this, a containment check that rejected everything would look
        exactly as green as one that works.

name: test_successful_build_produces_index_in_outdir
docstring: A normal build leaves artifacts in outdir, no staging dir leftover.

name: test_rebuild_preserves_vectors
docstring: After a rebuild, vectors.npy planted by an earlier embed must survive.

name: test_second_build_updates_manifest_build_id
docstring: Each build writes a fresh build_id; successive builds produce different IDs.

name: test_manifest_has_checksums
docstring: manifest.json must carry a non-empty checksums dict after a full build.

name: test_manifest_has_provenance_fields
docstring: manifest.json must carry build_id, tool_version, schema_version, created_at.

name: test_force_flag_allows_foreign_dir
docstring: --force lets build write into a non-r2g directory.

name: test_build_refuses_repo_root_as_outdir
docstring: build must raise SystemExit when -o points at the repo itself.

name: test_lock_timeout_flag_is_accepted
docstring: --lock-timeout is parsed without error (value consumed by cmd_build).

name: test_untrusted_checkout_fsmonitor_does_not_run_during_build
docstring:
#455: `ls-files`/`check-ignore` read the index, which runs the
    repository's own `core.fsmonitor` unless the invocation overrides it.

name: test_unwritable_lock_dir_fails_fast_with_the_real_cause
docstring:
#451 D9: a read-only mount used to wait the full timeout and then blame
    a lock holder that did not exist.

name: test_leftover_staging_and_backup_dirs_are_not_indexed
docstring:
#451 D7: a crash mid-swap leaves `.<out>.staging.*`/`.<out>.backup.*`
    holding a whole index; discovery must never treat it as source.

name: test_index_files_and_swap_are_fsynced
docstring:
#451 D5: an unflushed write survives a crash as an empty file that every
    "index exists" check accepts. Files and the swapped directories are synced.

name: test_ignored_directory_is_counted_once_not_walked
docstring:
#456 P6: without --directory, git enumerated every file under an ignored
    node_modules/venv on each build just to produce a count.

name: test_windows_junction_counts_as_a_link
docstring:
#451 D6: `is_symlink()` is False for an NTFS junction, so the output-path
    guard could be walked around with `mklink /J`.

name: test_swap_rename_retries_a_transient_windows_sharing_violation
docstring:
#451 D4: OneDrive or an AV scanner holding a file open made the swap fail
    hard with WinError 32, though the lock clears within a second.

name: test_git_discovery_failure_in_a_checkout_is_announced
docstring:
#453 S13: the walk fallback ignores .gitignore; when git fails inside a
    real checkout the file set silently changed.

name: test_tests_dimension_tracks_the_shipped_tests_edge
docstring:
The `Tests Link` dimension must describe `derived.add_tests_edges`.

    The generator used to hardcode "TESTS edge type not yet implemented",
    which cost all nineteen languages 10% of their weighted total for a
    feature that had already shipped, and which no test caught because
    `test_doc_consistency` only checks that the table matches the generator --
    both were wrong together. These three assertions each break one way of
    reintroducing that: the edge builder going missing, the notes going back
    to claiming it is unimplemented, and the CALLS dependency being dropped.

name: test_the_tool_specs_come_from_the_shipped_schemas
docstring: The eval must measure the descriptions this project actually ships.

name: test_every_eval_tool_is_a_real_dispatchable_tool
docstring: A typo here would silently shrink the measured surface.

name: _run
docstring:
Run the harness over `tasks_path`, indexing the sample fixture.

    `--index-out` is passed explicitly so the index lands under `tmp_path`.
    Without it the script used to default beside the tree it indexed, which
    left a `.r2g-llmeval/` inside `tests/fixtures/` after every run.

name: test_the_loop_dispatches_a_real_tool_against_a_real_index
docstring: End to end: scripted model -> dispatch -> scoring -> report.

name: test_the_scorer_is_not_vacuous
docstring:
A solvable task scores solved and an unsolvable one does not.

    Without this, a scorer that always returned False would look exactly like
    a weak model and could sit here indefinitely.

name: test_a_tool_error_is_handed_back_rather_than_crashing_the_run
docstring: A refused argument is something the model has to recover from.

name: test_the_report_carries_the_cost_of_the_run
docstring: A success rate with no cost beside it is not a usable number.

name: test_max_turns_is_enforced
docstring: A model that never stops calling tools must not loop forever.

name: _has_mcp
docstring:
A real, currently-*supported* SDK is importable.

    #407/#291 dropped mcp 1.x: `serve()` now speaks only the 2.x registration
    API (`on_list_tools=`/`on_call_tool=`), so a test that drives a live
    subprocess needs mcp>=2.0. This used to check
    `hasattr(Server, "list_tools")`, which is true only for the *unsupported*
    1.x generation -- so on any environment with the (now required) 2.x SDK
    installed, every test gated on it silently skipped forever. Detector:
    reverting this to the old hasattr check makes
    test_stdio_roundtrip_against_a_repo_with_no_index and
    test_stdi

name: _has_any_mcp
docstring:
Any `mcp` SDK is importable at all, supported or not.

    Only `test_tools_call_over_serve_completes_on_the_parallel_path` uses this -- it exercises `serve()`'s

    `_pool_stdio_probe.py` starts a pool with the exact kwargs `parse_all`
    passes, and has one worker write a sentinel to fd 1 and read a byte from
    fd 0. Measured on Windows (spawn) before the fix, a worker did both for
    real: the sentinel landed in the parent's stdout pipe and the worker
    consumed the byte the parent had queued -- which under `repo2graph-mcp`
    is a frame of the client's request stream the server then waits for
    forever.

    `timeout=` is the hard bound: a regression that hangs a worker on fd

name: test_tools_call_over_serve_completes_on_the_parallel_path

    The marker file is what makes this about the *parallel* path: the launcher
    records every ProcessPoolExecutor the server process builds, so a silent
    fall back to serial fails here rather than passing quietly.

    Timeouts everywhere -- a queue-fed reader thread, not a bare readline --
    because the bug being guarded is a hang, and a test that reproduces it
    with `proc.stdout.readline()` would never return.

    race each other through `atomic_write`, so the loser's work is discarded.
    The invocation count below is the detector: it reads 2 without the
    per-directory lock and 1 with it.

    BaseException, so an ordinary `except Exception` around the handler does not
    hold it -- this pins the conversion explicitly.

    `hmac.compare_digest` raises TypeError on a `str` carrying any non-ASCII
    character, and `latin-1` decodes every byte 0x80-0xFF into one. Because
    `AuthMiddleware` wraps the Starlette app from *outside*, Starlette's
    `ServerErrorMiddleware` never saw that exception -- it surfaced as an
    unhandled ASGI error an unauthenticated caller could trigger at will. The
    comparison is on bytes now, so this is an ordinary rejection.

An ambiguous 1-of-3 CALLS edge on the path must show as the minimum,
    not be hidden by a later confident hop.

name: _flood_star
docstring:
`n` direct CALLS neighbours hanging off `hub_id`, none of them the
    eventual target -- so a *single* hop already exceeds MCP_MAX_PATH_VISITED,
    proving the visited cap binds independently of the hop budget.

name: test_path_between_visited_ceiling_actually_binds_under_flood
docstring:
A hub with far more direct neighbours than MCP_MAX_PATH_VISITED, none
    of them the (unreachable) target, must report `truncated` rather than
    silently exploring the whole fan-out -- proving the visited cap binds
    on its own, not merely the hop cap (CONTRIBUTING.md: a hop bound alone does
    not bound work on a dense graph).

name: test_blast_radius_reverse_calls_closure_goes_multiple_hops
docstring:
Callers of callers, not just one hop -- the distinction from
    repo_neighbours (#387).

name: test_blast_radius_never_returns_a_secret_neighbour
docstring:
The secret filter rule extended: a caller/importer that lives at a secret path
    must not appear even though it is graph-reachable.

name: test_blast_radius_a_hub_symbol_reports_truncated_not_a_partial_set_as_complete
docstring:
Acceptance: hitting the visited ceiling says so rather than silently
    returning a subset that reads as the full picture.

name: test_path_between_paths_limit_is_clamped_in_the_handler
docstring:
`max_paths` above MCP_MAX_PATHS must not widen the traversal.

    Nothing exercised this clamp, so deleting it would have let a caller ask for
    an unbounded number of paths. Asserted where the value is consumed --
    `_reconstruct`'s `cap` -- rather than by counting returned paths: the
    bidirectional search reconstructs through one meeting node, so how many
    paths a fixture yields is a property of the graph shape, not of the ceiling.

name: test_repo_search_forwards_every_advertised_parameter
docstring:
Whatever the schema advertises must reach the tool.

    The dispatcher once dropped `neighbours`/`max_neighbours` while the schema
    still advertised them, so a client setting `neighbours="cite"` got full-body
    neighbours and no error. Asserted against the schema rather than a
    hand-written list, so a newly advertised parameter that is not forwarded
    fails here.

    Those two parameters are now retired rather than silently dropped: see
    `test_retired_retrieval_parameters_are_neither_advertised_nor_forwarded`.

name: test_retired_retrieval_parameters_are_neither_advertised_nor_forwarded
docstring:
Citation mode is retired over MCP, and must not be reachable by accident.

    On 40 held-out lexical and 40 held-out structural questions, `cite`
    neighbours measured -1/-8/-19 pp and -3/-10/-31 pp against the default, and
    were dominated by turning expansion off entirely -- better recall for fewer
    tokens. An agent picks its arguments out of the schema, so advertising a
    dominated mode is how it gets chosen.

    Unadvertised *and* unforwarded is the point. Advertised-but-inert is the
    defect this file already records having fixed once.

name: FakeNeo4j
docstring: Records each transactional request; can be told to fail the Nth.

name: test_launcher_spawns_batch_shims_through_a_shell
docstring:
Static guard on the EINVAL fix, so a future edit that drops `shell` fails here.

    Asserts the source still pairs a `.cmd`/`.bat` check with a `shell` option
    -- the behavioural test below is the real detector, but this one also runs
    on a machine with no Node.js at all.

name: _run_launcher
signature: def _run_launcher(tmp_path: Path, shim_dir: Path, args: list[str]) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
docstring:
Run the launcher with PATH pointing only at `shim_dir`.

    Bytes, never `text=True`: the same decoding discipline CONTRIBUTING.md requires
    for git subprocesses applies to any non-ASCII a shim might echo on a
    cp1252 Windows locale.

name: _write_uvx_shim
docstring:
A fake `uvx` on PATH that echoes its argv and exits 0.

    A `.cmd` on Windows -- which is precisely the shape that used to fail --
    and a plain shell script elsewhere.

name: test_launcher_runs_a_uvx_shim_on_path
docstring:
The launcher finds `uvx` and hands off to it, exiting with its status.

    On Windows the shim is a `.cmd`, so this fails with EINVAL and a non-zero
    exit if `run()` ever goes back to spawning a resolved path directly.

name: test_launcher_propagates_the_child_exit_status
docstring: A non-zero exit from the underlying server is the launcher's own exit code.

name: test_launcher_forwards_an_argument_containing_spaces
docstring:
A repository path with a space survives the Windows shell hand-off.

    `shell: true` re-parses the command line, so an unquoted argument would
    arrive at the shim split in two. This is the case quoting exists for.

name: test_launcher_explains_itself_when_no_python_launcher_is_installed
docstring: With an empty PATH the launcher must not install anything -- it explains and exits 1.

name: test_launcher_refuses_a_batch_shim_it_cannot_quote_for
docstring:
`%`, `!` and `"` have no in-band escape on a `shell: true` cmd.exe line.

    `quoteForCmd` wraps an argument in double quotes, but cmd.exe still expands
    `%VAR%` and (under delayed expansion) `!VAR!` *inside* quotes, and it honours
    no backslash escape for an embedded `"` -- `\\"` is a C-runtime convention,
    not a cmd.exe one, so the `"`-escaping in `quoteForCmd` is a no-op there.
    Rather than hand cmd.exe a line it will mangle, `run()` refuses.

    Deliberately asserts opposite outcomes per platform, because the gate is
    reached only via `needsShell`, which is `win32 && (.cmd

name: test_the_launcher_is_published_from_the_release_tag_after_pypi
docstring:
#399: npm ships from the same publish.yml run as PyPI, after it, with provenance,
    and cannot hold up the GitHub Release.

name: indexed
docstring: A fixture repo whose every edge type has a known, checkable location.

name: test_every_edge_has_type_method_confidence_and_evidence
docstring: The failure this schema replaces: four of six types were bare triples.

name: test_field_order_is_stable
docstring:
`edges.jsonl` is a committable artifact whose diff humans read; a field
    that moves between lines makes every edge look changed.

name: test_evidence_points_at_the_line_that_proves_the_edge
docstring:
A citation is only worth having if opening it shows the relationship.

    Hand-derived from the fixture source above, then read back off disk --
    never taken from what the builder produced.

name: test_structural_edges_have_no_fabricated_evidence
docstring:
A file being in a directory is not written anywhere. Claiming a line
    for it would be exactly the fabricated citation this schema prevents.

name: test_call_edges_are_attributed_to_the_resolver
docstring:
The parse tree supplies a name; matching it to a definition is the
    resolver's judgement, and that is where ambiguity comes from.

name: test_defines_records_the_grammar_that_read_it
docstring:
`tree-sitter/python` not bare `tree-sitter`: the same edge type carries
    different weight from different grammars.

name: test_ambiguous_calls_split_confidence_across_candidates
docstring: Two definitions of one name: each edge gets 1/n, and says so.

name: test_cochange_is_marked_correlational
docstring: git-log edges must not be mistaken for structural ones.

name: test_limitations_block_has_the_same_shape_even_with_nothing_to_caveat
docstring: A section that appears only when something is wrong gets skipped.

name: test_limitations_block_reports_truncation
docstring:
An answer from a truncated pack can be wrong by omission, and nothing
    else in the output says so.

name: test_limitations_block_is_pure_ascii
docstring:
It is written to a console that may be a strict cp1252 stream on
    Windows, where an em dash is a crash rather than a typographic nicety.

name: test_answer_appends_the_segment
docstring: The segment is appended by repo2graph, not produced by the model.

name: _Lines
docstring: Stands in for _BoundedLines; the caller asks it for both bound flags.

name: test_bundle_never_contains_source_code
docstring:
The one absolute rule. A user filing from a private repository must be
    able to post this without reading every line of it first.

name: test_bundle_contains_no_absolute_paths
docstring:
Absolute paths carry usernames, home layout and employer directory
    conventions, and add nothing once the repo-relative path is known.

name: test_bundle_carries_the_edge_quality_histogram
docstring:
Often what explains a bad answer: a graph dominated by ambiguous name
    matches behaves differently from one that resolves cleanly.

name: test_bundle_survives_a_missing_index
docstring: A user whose build failed still needs to file a report.

name: test_every_category_has_an_issue_template
docstring: `--category` and the GitHub template chooser must not drift apart.

name: test_mcp_neighbours_cites_the_call_site_not_just_the_definition
docstring:
For "what calls this", the useful citation is the call site.

    The node label says where the *neighbour* is defined; the edge's evidence
    says where the relationship is written. `repo_neighbours` must carry both,
    or an agent asking for callers gets a list of definitions with no way to
    open the lines that actually do the calling.

name: test_mcp_neighbours_marks_an_ambiguous_edge
docstring:
An edge below 1.0 must not read like a certain one.

    Without the marker, a name that matched three candidates is presented to
    the agent exactly as a unique resolution is -- which is the trust problem
    the edge schema exists to fix, on the one surface an agent actually reads.

name: test_mcp_search_returns_cited_markdown
docstring: `repo_search` returns the pack's markdown, headers and all.

name: test_mcp_tools_return_text_not_json
docstring:
Pinned because docs/architecture.md documents the citation *form* per
    surface, and it previously claimed these returned per-result `path` and
    `start_line` fields. They return strings.

name: test_bundle_scrubs_paths_out_of_free_text_notes
docstring:
Prose assembled elsewhere must not be able to smuggle a path in.

    `compute_freshness` interpolates an exception message into a note, and an
    `OSError` carries the absolute path that failed -- so a discovery failure
    put an absolute path to `pkg/secret_roadmap.py` into a bundle that
    promises no absolute paths and no filenames. The happy path produces no
    such note, which is why the other privacy tests did not see it.

    Scrubbed at the boundary rather than in each producer: the guarantee has
    to hold for prose written by code that has never heard of the bundle.

name: _pyproject
docstring:
Parse pyproject.toml, or skip where the stdlib cannot.

    `tomllib` is 3.11+ and `requires-python` is `>=3.10`, so a module-level
    `import tomllib` made the whole file an import error on the declared floor
    -- collection failed before any test ran. The rest of the suite already
    handles this by importing inside the function and skipping (see
    `test_compat.py` and `test_grammar_availability.py`); adding `tomli` just
    for this would be a new dependency on the floor the package promises.

name: test_the_py_typed_marker_exists
docstring:
PEP 561: without this file, inline annotations are invisible downstream.

    `[tool.mypy] strict = true` checks this package's own source. It says
    nothing about what a *consumer* of `docs/python-api.md`'s API sees, because
    a type checker ignores annotations in an installed package that ships no
    marker -- so every public function read as returning `Any` however strictly
    it was checked here.

name: test_py_typed_is_declared_as_package_data
docstring:
The marker has to be in the wheel, not merely in the repository.

    `[tool.setuptools.packages.find]` collects `.py` files only, so a `py.typed`
    sitting in the source tree is silently dropped from the built distribution
    without this declaration -- the failure mode is invisible locally and only
    shows up for someone who `pip install`s the package.

name: test_requires_python_matches_the_declared_classifiers
docstring:
A classifier promising a version `requires-python` excludes is a lie.

    Both are read by installers and by PyPI's own filtering, and they drift in
    opposite directions: a new interpreter gets added to the CI matrix and the
    classifiers, and the floor gets raised, and nothing cross-checks them.

name: test_the_default_parse_budget_leaves_room_for_the_slowest_real_file
docstring:
The budget is a static promise, so assert it statically.

    The slowest real file across the five benchmark corpora took 0.74 s, so the
    10 s default is a >13x margin. This used to be checked by parsing a deep
    fixture under the default budget and asserting it was not flagged -- which
    made the runner's speed part of the assertion and failed intermittently on
    a contended CI box (seen on ubuntu/3.12 under `-n auto --cov`). The margin
    is what the test is really about, and it does not need a stopwatch.

name: test_a_deep_legitimate_file_is_not_a_false_positive
docstring:
Deep-but-ordinary content must not trip the runaway heuristic.

    The budget here is explicit and generous rather than the default, because
    what is under test is the *content* -- 425 KB of literals nested 200 deep
    parses in ~0.8 s on a developer machine -- not how fast the runner is
    today. See `test_the_default_parse_budget_leaves_room_for_the_slowest_real_file`
    for the margin the default actually carries.

name: test_strict_policy_fails_instead_of_skipping
signature:
def test_strict_policy_fails_instead_of_skipping(tmp_path):
    # Either bound, for the reason given in
    # `test_a_runaway_parse_is_stopped_and_counted`: what strict policy promises
    # is that a skip becomes an error naming the file, not which bound caught it.

name: test_an_in_process_parse_over_budget_is_discarded_too
docstring:
Small files in a serial build parse in-process, where the budget can only
    discard the result afterwards; the outcome is the same as a kill.

name: slow
test_a_parse_that_exhausts_worker_memory_is_a_crash_not_an_oom
signature:
def test_a_parse_that_exhausts_worker_memory_is_a_crash_not_an_oom(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    # The runaway input needs hundreds of MB, far over a 64 MB cap, and far
    # under the time budget.
    # The cap is read in the parent and handed to each worker, so patching it
    # here reaches workers

name: test_windows_cap_memory_invoked_on_win32
docstring: parsepool._cap_memory binds worker process to Windows Job Object with memory limit.

name: _read_lines
docstring: Read file using split('\n') per AGENTS.md text slicing rule.

name: test_prod_igy_workflow_structure
docstring: Verify that prod-igy.yml is well-formed and meets security/repo requirements.

name: test_prod_igy_script_exists_and_exports
docstring: Verify that prod-igy.js exists and exports expected functions and constants.

name: test_prod_igy_label_definitions
docstring: Verify all label definitions have valid hex colors and descriptions.

name: test_prod_igy_calculate_size_logic
docstring: Verify size thresholds in calculateSize implementation.

name: test_prod_igy_type_detection_regexes
docstring: Verify regexes used for conventional commit type detection.

name: test_prod_igy_detect_areas_patterns
docstring: Verify that detectAreas covers all critical repository subsystems.

name: test_prod_igy_area_patterns_name_paths_that_exist
docstring:
Every `repo2graph/...` path prod-igy matches on must still be in the tree.

    `area/walker` pointed at `repo2graph/walker.py` and `area/mcp` at
    `repo2graph/mcp.py` long after the first was deleted (8ef6d006) and the
    second became a package (c8c20bdb), so neither label could ever be applied
    again and nothing failed. The assertions above pinned the stale strings,
    which is what let it sit. This checks the paths against the filesystem
    instead, so the next rename fails here rather than going quiet in CI.

name: test_prod_igy_issue_extraction_regex
docstring: Verify the issue extraction regex matches action words and issue numbers.

name: test_prod_igy_invariant_guidance_cites_contributing
docstring:
Verify the invariant rule strings in checkRepositoryInvariants.

    The rules used to cite `AGENTS.md`, which was removed in 58c1f833 when the
    technical invariants moved into CONTRIBUTING.md. Every citation must name a
    file that is actually in the repository, or the checklist prod-igy posts on
    every PR points a contributor at nothing.

name: test_prod_igy_comment_formatting_and_author_tagging
docstring: Verify that comment formatting contains @<author> tags and required commands.

name: test_issue_comment_job_requires_trusted_author_association
docstring:
Issue #208: outsider PR comments must not start the privileged triage job.

    The gate lives in the workflow `if:` so no runner is allocated. Trusted
    associations are the three GitHub values for people who can change the
    repo; CONTRIBUTOR / NONE / FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR are not among them.

name: test_script_issue_comment_skips_untrusted_association
docstring: Issue #208: script defence if the workflow `if:` is ever widened.

name: test_format_bot_comment_strips_backticks_from_refs
docstring:
Issue #208: a fork branch name must not break out of a markdown code span.

    git check-ref-format permits `` ` ``. The Head Commit line (and every
    other `` `${headRef}` `` / `` `${baseRef}` `` interpolation) wraps the
    ref in backticks; closing that span plants attacker markdown under the
    bot identity. SHA slices stay raw — they are not attacker-controlled
    the same way.

name: test_prod_igy_auto_retargets_main_to_develop
docstring: Verify that prod-igy automatically retargets PRs from main to develop and posts notice.

name: _js_regex
signature: def _js_regex(content: str, name: str, arg: str) -> re.Pattern:
docstring:
Pull a `const <name> = /<pattern>/i.test(<arg>)` literal out of the script.

    The retarget guard is the one piece of prod-igy whose *behaviour* is worth
    asserting rather than its source text, and the pytest environment has no
    Node (see this module's docstring). Extracting the literal and compiling it
    with `re` tests the pattern itself: a typo in the login shape fails here
    instead of silently retargeting a release PR in production.

name: test_prod_igy_never_retargets_a_release_pr
docstring:
A release PR must stay on `main`.

    publish.yml has prod-igy raise `release/vX.Y.Z -> main` and then polls for
    that merge, so retargeting it to `develop` strands the version bump and
    times the release run out with nothing merged.

name: test_no_standalone_claude_review_workflows_remain
docstring:
The claude-code-action workflows are gone and must not come back.

    They were the two automated-code-review surfaces. `claude.yml` in
    particular let *any* commenter start a 30-minute model run with no
    author_association gate at all -- the exact hole prod-igy's
    TRUSTED_ASSOCIATIONS closes on its own comment path.

name: test_no_contributor_invokable_ai_path
docstring:
No workflow may start a model run from untrusted comment text.

    A contributor must not be able to address the AI. The only mention-driven
    trigger left in the repository is prod-igy's `@prod-igy`, gated on
    author_association in both the workflow `if:` and the script.

name: test_ai_workflow_wiring
docstring: The AI step's inputs come from the base checkout, and default to off.

name: test_ai_env_flag_is_case_folded
docstring:
AGENTS.md truthiness rule, applied to the AI gate.

    GitHub's `env.PRODIGY_AI == 'true'` matches 'True' and 'TRUE'. If the JS
    side used a bare `=== 'true'`, a variable set to 'True' would install the
    SDK and then skip the AI step -- the same split-gate bug as action.yml's
    embed/rag seam, and equally invisible to a Python-only suite.

name: test_ai_ledger_round_trip_and_hostile_input
docstring: Per-PR spend survives a comment rewrite and degrades to zero, never up.

name: _sanitize_model
docstring:
Python model of prod-igy.js `sanitizeAiText`, rule for rule, in order.

    The tests below pin each JS line verbatim *and* exercise this model, so a
    rule deleted from the JS fails a pin and a rule that stops working fails
    the behaviour. Keep the two in step.

name: test_ai_text_cannot_forge_a_marker_or_a_mention
docstring:
Model output is contributor-derived and rendered under the bot identity.

    Two concrete failures this prevents:
      - a second BOT_MARKER in the prose makes `comments.find()` return the
        model's text forever, so prod-igy never finds its real comment again;
      - a mention pings a real account from an App that holds issues:write.

name: test_ai_text_strips_markdown_images_and_links
docstring: #373: markdown image/link syntax must not survive into the comment. `![](url)` is fetched server-side by GitHub's camo proxy the moment the comment renders -- a request to an attacker-controlled host that confirms the workflow ran and when. `[text](url)`, a reference-style `[label]: url` definition, an autolink, and an HTML `` are all the same reviewer-phishing primitive under a trusted bot identity. Adversarial inputs: reference-style links, nested brackets, `![]()`, autolinks, HTML ``, and a URL that smuggles a token in its query string.

name: test_ai_text_neutralises_protocol_relative_and_entity_encoded_links
test_summary_step_does_exactly_two_things
docstring:
The schema is the whole contract, and it has two fields.

    Labels stay path- and size-derived: `detectType`, `detectAreas` and
    `calculateSize` are exact, and a model guess that contradicted them would
    make a label mean "computed" on some PRs and "guessed" on others with
    nothing in the comment to say which. Review, risk assessment and anything
    requiring knowledge of code outside the diff are out of scope by
    construction -- there is no field to put them in.

name: test_summary_step_is_not_shown_the_codebase
docstring:
It sees one diff. It is not given repository rules or any other file.

    Feeding CONTRIBUTING.md (or any repo content) to the model is what turns a
    description into a review, which is the thing this bot deliberately does
    not do. The rule checklist in the comment stays where it was: derived from
    changed paths by `checkRepositoryInvariants`, with no model involved.

name: test_check_results_come_from_the_api_not_the_model
docstring:
"What tests passed" must be read, never guessed.

    A model asked to comment on tests would answer from the diff, which says
    nothing about whether CI actually ran. The counts come from
    `checks.listForRef` on the PR head, and the model is told to stay off the
    subject so its prose cannot contradict them.

name: test_ai_caps_are_checked_before_the_call
docstring:
Both ceilings gate the request, not the bookkeeping after it.

    `synchronize` fires on every push, so without a run cap a force-push loop
    is an unbounded bill. A cap checked after the call bounds nothing.

name: test_ai_failure_falls_back_to_the_pre_ai_behaviour
docstring:
Every failure mode returns `{ai: null, reason}` -- none of them throws.

    prod-igy worked before the AI step existed and must keep working when the
    model is unreachable, the key is revoked, or the SDK never installed. This
    is the same zero-dependency floor the rest of the repo keeps (BM25 under
    vectors, inline rules under AGENTS.md).

name: test_ai_workflow_survives_a_registry_outage
docstring: A failed `npm install` must not fail the triage job.

name: test_degraded_run_is_invisible_to_the_contributor
docstring:
With no summary, the comment is the ordinary inspection and says nothing.

    The degraded path must not announce itself. A contributor reading a PR
    where the summary could not be produced sees exactly the comment prod-igy
    posted before the summary section existed -- no banner, no apology, no
    reference to anything having been skipped. The reason is recorded for the
    maintainer in the run log instead.

name: test_comment_never_discloses_how_the_summary_is_produced
docstring:
No machine-provenance language reaches a contributor-visible string.

    The comment carries prod-igy's bot identity in its heading and that is the
    whole of the disclosure. Naming a model, a confidence score, or a fallback
    in the prose makes the comment worse to read and is not what the heading
    already communicates.

name: test_summary_routes_back_to_the_reviewer
docstring:
The summary section tags a human, and the title is suggested, not applied.

    The cc is the buffer: every PR that gets a summary puts it in front of the
    maintainer. It reads as an ordinary hand-off, which is all it needs to be.

name: test_ai_prompt_frames_pr_text_as_data
docstring: The PR body and diff are contributor-controlled and reach the model.

name: test_edited_does_not_retrigger_the_privileged_job
docstring:
#374: `edited` fires whenever a PR's title or body changes -- which the
    author (including a fork author) controls and can pull at will, against a
    job holding pull-requests: write, issues: write and an API key. It must
    not be in the trigger's `types:` list.

name: test_app_token_probe_env_is_job_level_not_step_level
docstring:
#375: the app-token step's `if:` used to read `env.HAS_APP_ID` /
    `env.HAS_PRIVATE_KEY` from an `env:` block declared on that same step,
    which works only if the step's own `env:` is guaranteed resolved before
    its `if:` evaluates -- behaviour GitHub documents loosely. Promoting the
    probes to job level removes the ordering question: every step's `if:`
    reads the same job-level env the normal way.

name: test_the_fallback_identity_is_logged
docstring:
#375 (acceptance): the GITHUB_TOKEN fallback is no longer silent --
    a run log line says which identity is posting.

name: test_github_app_token_is_scoped_to_the_job_permissions
docstring:
The app token must not inherit the App installation's full permission
    grant: each `permission-<name>` input narrows it to something the job
    actually does, and never to more than the job's own `permissions:` block.

    `permission-issues` and `permission-checks` must NOT come back.
    `permission-*` requests that exact set and the API answers 422 "The
    permissions requested are not granted to this installation" when any one of
    them is absent from the installation's grant -- so an extra entry mints
    nothing at all rather than a slightly wider token, and the job silently falls

name: test_ai_diff_budget_is_per_file
docstring:
One generated file must not consume the whole diff allowance.

    Concatenate-then-truncate would let a single 50k-line lockfile or vendored
    blob push every other file out of the context, so the model would summarise
    a change it never saw.

name: test_zizmor_ignore_pins_still_point_at_what_they_suppress
docstring:
`.github/zizmor.yml` suppresses findings by `file:line`.

    Its own header says a shifted line number un-ignores the finding rather than
    silently keeping it suppressed -- but the reverse is worse and just as quiet:
    an edit above a pinned line slides the pin onto unrelated YAML, where it
    suppresses whatever finding lands there next. Only zizmor itself can prove a
    pin still matches, and zizmor is not a dependency of the pytest environment,
    so this pins the *construct* each entry was written for.

    The window is **per pin and tight**, which is the whole detector. An earli

name: test_existing_bot_comment_filters_on_bot_author
docstring:
