name: test_decoding_arbitrary_bytes_never_raises_and_never_moves_a_line_boundary
docstring:
Detects a decode that invents or swallows a newline, desyncing every citation.

    `graph._chunk_and_parse` counts newlines on the *raw bytes* (`newlines +=
    chunk.count(b"\\n")`) and then hands the *decoded text* to the parser, whose
    rows are what every `start_line`/`end_line` in nodes.jsonl is built from. If
    those two counts can ever disagree -- a replacement character that is a
    newline, a stray 0x0A consumed as part of a multi-byte sequence -- every
    symbol below that point is cited at the wrong line and nothing in the
    pipeline notices.

    An example test can only a

name: test_the_carried_utf8_tail_is_bounded_and_never_holds_a_newline
docstring:
Detects a carry that would double-count a line across a slice boundary.

    `_incomplete_utf8_tail`'s docstring promises two things the caller depends
    on and neither is checked anywhere else: the carry is at most three bytes
    (the longest truncated prefix of a four-byte sequence), and it "never
    [contains] a newline ... so `line_offset` accounting is unaffected". If a
    newline could ride along in the carry it would be counted once in the slice
    that produced it and again in the slice that consumed it, shifting
    `line_offset` -- and so every symbol in a chunked file -- by on

name: test_carrying_the_utf8_tail_across_a_slice_boundary_loses_no_characters
docstring:
Detects the two-slices-both-dropped bug `_incomplete_utf8_tail` exists to fix.

    Slices are cut at raw byte offsets, so a multi-byte character straddles the
    boundary: its lead byte ends slice N and its continuations begin slice N+1.
    Before the carry, *both* slices failed to decode and both were discarded --
    up to 2 x max_file_bytes of source lost silently. The property is that
    re-splitting at the carry-adjusted offset reproduces the original text
    exactly, for every cut point in every string.

    An example can only pick one cut point in one string, and the cut points

name: test_encodable_output_is_writable_for_arbitrary_text
docstring:
Detects a guard that lets an unrepresentable character reach a strict stream.

    `tests/test_encoding.py` runs this cross product over five hand-picked
    characters. Those five were each added after a crash report, which is the
    tell: the matrix covers the failures that already happened. Hypothesis
    covers the ones that have not, including strings mixing a lone surrogate
    with U+2028 and CJK in one line -- the combination no reporter has sent in
    yet and the one where `encodable`'s encode/decode round trip is most likely
    to produce something the codec still refuses.

name: test_lines_counts_rows_exactly_the_way_tree_sitter_does
docstring:
Detects a reintroduced `splitlines()` in the one helper that must not use it.

    CONTRIBUTING invariant 1: tree-sitter advances `Point.row` strictly on
    "\\n", so `_lines` must too. The property that pins it is arithmetic rather
    than exemplary -- the row count is always `src.count("\\n") + 1`, never
    anything derived from the characters in between -- and the second assertion
    states the failure mode directly: a source with no "\\n" at all is one line,
    however many U+2028s or form feeds it contains.

    An example only detects a `splitlines()` regression if its fixture happe

name: test_keepends_lf_is_lossless_and_breaks_only_on_lf
docstring:
Detects a lossy chunk split -- source text silently dropped from an artifact.

    `_split` rebuilds every chunk by joining `_keepends_lf` output, so
    `"".join(_keepends_lf(t)) == t` is the invariant that stands between the
    chunker and quietly losing a line of the user's code. It is stated in the
    docstring and was never tested against anything but LF-only ASCII.

    The exotic break characters matter here for a second reason beyond line
    numbering: `splitlines(keepends=True)` would make a chunk's *pieces* depend
    on whichever stray separators the source happens to hold, so th

name: test_a_one_indexed_inclusive_line_slice_round_trips
docstring:
Detects an off-by-one in the `[start_line, end_line]` slice every chunk uses.

    `chunks.iter_chunks` cuts a symbol body with
    `"\\n".join(lines[start_line - 1 : end_line])` -- 1-indexed, inclusive at
    both ends. The property is that the slice re-splits into exactly the lines
    it was cut from and into exactly `end - start + 1` of them, for every valid
    range in every text. A fixture with a 3-line function and a hand-counted
    expectation tests one range; the boundary cases (a single line, the first
    line, the last line, a range ending on a trailing empty line) are where the

name: test_split_covers_every_line_with_overlap_and_no_gap
docstring:
Detects a line dropped between two chunk slices, or a slicer that never ends.

    `_split`'s packer rewinds by `OVERLAP_LINES` between slices
    (`i = max(start + 1, i - OVERLAP_LINES)`). That one expression has to do two
    incompatible things at once: rewind far enough to overlap, and still
    guarantee forward progress when a slice held fewer lines than the overlap.
    Get it wrong one way and a line vanishes from every artifact; get it wrong
    the other and the loop never terminates.

    Each generated line is prefixed with its own index, so a slice can be mapped
    back to the li

name: test_split_bounds_a_line_that_cannot_be_split_on_a_line_boundary
docstring:
Detects an unbounded chunk from minified JS, base64 or one-line JSON.

    A single line longer than `max_chars` cannot be shrunk by grouping on line
    boundaries, so `_split` pre-breaks it into `max_chars`-sized pieces. Without
    that step the packer emits the whole line as one slice, unbounded -- the
    retrieval budget is then silently exceeded by a chunk nobody can page past.

    The two halves of the guarantee are tested together because they trade off:
    bounding every slice is easy if you are allowed to lose characters, and
    keeping every character is easy if you are allowed

name: test_redaction_never_changes_the_line_count
docstring:
Detects redaction that shifts every citation below a secret.

    `chunks.iter_chunks` scans and redacts the whole body *before* splitting,
    and its comment states the reason that is safe: "Redaction is
    line-preserving, so splitting afterwards keeps every citation line number
    intact." `redact_content` implements that by re-appending `text.count("\\n",
    start, end)` newlines to each replacement. If a single span ever lost or
    gained one, every `[cite: path:start-end]` below it in the file would point
    at the wrong code, and the citation would still look well-formed.

name: test_redaction_of_arbitrary_text_preserves_the_line_count
docstring:
Same invariant, but over text whose line breaks are the exotic ones.

    Split out from the generated-secrets test because it fails differently: here

    that treats U+2028 as a line terminator while `_lines` does not, so the two
    disagree about which line a finding is on.

name: test_a_non_redacting_policy_returns_the_text_untouched

Detects a policy switch that quietly rewrites text it was told to leave alone.

name: test_secret_path_detection_is_separator_invariant
docstring:
Detects a Windows-spelled path that dodges the secret-file refusal.

    `_is_secret_path` is the gate that keeps `.env`, `*.pem` and `secrets/` out
    of an index, and it normalizes with `str(path).replace("\\\\", "/")` before
    deciding. If any later comparison in that function is made against the
    un-normalized string, the same file is refused when written `secrets/db.key`
    and indexed when written `secrets\\db.key` -- a credential in chunks.jsonl,
    reachable from every MCP tool, on exactly one platform.

    Example tests spell their fixtures with forward slashes because that i

name: test_secret_path_detection_is_idempotent_under_renormalization
docstring:
Detects a verdict that depends on how many times a path has been normalized.

    Paths reach this function from several directions -- `parse.discover` hands
    it `rel.as_posix()`, the MCP `repo_read` path hands it a caller-supplied
    string it has already slash-normalized itself -- so the same file is checked
    in more than one spelling within a single request. Normalizing again must
    not change the answer; if it does, which spelling arrived first decides
    whether a secret is served.

    This is the `normalize(normalize(p)) == normalize(p)` property stated at the
    level that m

name: test_secret_path_detection_is_case_invariant
docstring:
Detects a case-sensitive comparison in a check that claims to lowercase.

    Windows and macOS filesystems are case-insensitive by default, so `.ENV` and
    `.env` are the same file. `_is_secret_path` lowercases up front for exactly
    that reason, and the risk is a later branch comparing against the original.
    `appsettings.Production.json` is in the segment pool on purpose: it is
    matched by a regex rather than by an exact name, which is the branch most
    likely to be written against the un-lowercased text.

name: test_test_path_detection_is_separator_invariant
docstring:
Detects `latest.py` being re-classified as a test, or a test file missed.

    `is_test_path`'s docstring records the bug it was written to fix: a suffix
    match on `"test.py"` classified `latest.py`, `fastest.py` and `manifest.py`
    as tests, which excluded them from `is_public_symbol` and credited them as
    their own coverage. The fix matches per path *component*, which makes the
    function depend entirely on splitting the path correctly -- so the separator
    spelling is now load-bearing, and both spellings reach it (`impact` reads
    paths from a diff, which on Windows can carry

name: test_explain_path_never_reports_an_escaping_path_as_included
docstring:
Detects a `..` that walks out of the repo and still answers INCLUDED.

    `explain_path` is the documented answer to "would repo2graph index this
    file", and `repo2graph explain-path` feeds it whatever the user typed. It
    resolves the *parent* only (so a leaf symlink is still rejected by
    `discover`'s lstat) and relies on `relative_to(root)` to catch everything
    else. The property is the one that makes it a boundary rather than a
    convenience: if the verdict is INCLUDED, the reported relative path must not
    be absolute, and must still land under the root once resolved.

name: test_explain_path_verdict_is_idempotent_on_its_own_output
docstring:
Detects a normalizer whose output it would itself answer differently about.

    `explain_path` returns `relative_path` as the canonical spelling of what it
    was asked about. Feeding that back in has to produce the same verdict and
    the same rule, or the CLI's own output is not a valid input to the CLI --
    which is how a user reports "it says excluded, but when I paste the path it
    says included".

    This is `normalize(normalize(p)) == normalize(p)` for the one function in
    the codebase that publishes its normalized form.

name: test_a_trailing_dotdot_cannot_launder_an_excluded_path
docstring:
Detects an exclusion rule defeated by respelling the path.

    The verdict `explain_path` gives for a file must not depend on which of the
    infinitely many spellings of that file the caller typed. `F`, `F/x/..` and
    `F/x/y/../..` all name `F`, so all three must get `F`'s answer -- otherwise
    the rule that refuses to index credentials is advisory rather than binding,
    and the function that exists to explain the rules misreports them.

    Hand-written examples missed this for the ordinary reason: they spell paths
    the way the rest of the codebase produces them (`rel.as_posix()`

name: test_parse_spec_never_yields_a_component_that_escapes_the_clone_directory
docstring:
Detects a repo spec that makes `git clone` write outside its temp directory.

    `fetch.parse_spec` feeds `owner` and `repo` straight into a clone
    destination and into a `git` argv, so a component of `..` targets the parent
    of the temp dir and a component starting with `-` is read by git as an
    option. The function's own comment names both. The property asserts the
    consequence rather than the implementation: whatever comes back, joining it
    under a base directory and normalizing must stay under that base, and
    neither component may be option-shaped.

    A validator built

name: test_parse_ref_never_yields_a_ref_git_would_read_as_an_option
docstring:
Detects a refname that smuggles a flag or a traversal into a `git` argv.

    `parse_ref`'s comment is explicit that the pattern is "a security check and
    not just a spelling check", and names the exact hazards: a leading `-`, a
    dotted traversal component, a trailing newline that a `$`-anchored pattern
    would have let through. Each of those was a separate hand-written example.
    The property covers them as one statement -- whatever is returned contains
    no `..`, no separator-adjacent dot component, no whitespace and no leading
    dash -- and keeps covering the ones not yet thou

    The `_split` properties drive `max_chars` between 24 and 120 to keep the
    examples small. If `MAX_CHARS` ever drops into that range the production
    default would be inside the generated band rather than above it, and the
    properties would stop saying anything about the shipped configuration.

name: test_fit_lines_is_linear_not_quadratic
docstring:
Detector for fit_lines linearity. The old implementation called `measure` once
        per line either way -- the quadratic cost was in the *string building*,
        which no call counter can see -- so this has to be a wall-clock test.

        Comparing one input size against a larger one does not work here: the
        ceiling would be anchored on a small-input timing that is itself
        quadratic, and the two grow together. Measured, a 10x spread separates
        the regression from the allowance by only ~2x, which is how a timing
        test becomes a flake on a shared runner.

docstring: Verify build / query / map / stats keep working exactly as before.

name: FakeResponse
docstring: Minimal stand-in for the object urlopen returns.

name: FakeOpener
docstring:
Stand-in for `answer._OPENER`, delegating to a urlopen-shaped callable.

    `stream_answer` goes through an opener rather than `urlopen` so that its
    redirect handler cannot be bypassed (`_SameOriginRedirect`); patching the
    opener is what keeps these tests off the network.

name: test_grounded_prompt_and_citations_reach_the_endpoint
docstring:
Verify the request body carries the grounding rules and the pack; the
    only host contacted is the provider's -- nothing real is dialled.

name: test_real_urllib_path_against_a_localhost_server
docstring: Verify the same contract over a real socket, 127.0.0.1 only.

name: test_no_provider_env_names_all_four_variables
docstring: Verify the SystemExit message lists every supported env var.

name: test_cp1252_stdout_never_raises_unicodeencodeerror
docstring: Verify non-ASCII model output survives a cp1252 console.

name: test_writer_uses_stdout_text_not_buffer_bytes
docstring:
Verify _writer(None) must write through sys.stdout's text `write`,
    never through sys.stdout.buffer. Writing raw UTF-8 bytes straight to the
    buffer bypasses TextIOWrapper's console codepage translation on Windows,
    producing mojibake with no exception raised.

name: test_emit_surrogateescape_and_lookup_error
docstring: S-12/S-13: _emit preserves surrogateescape and survives LookupError.

name: _stub_dns
docstring:
Pin name resolution, so the SSRF guard's verdict is not the DNS's.

    `_is_blocked_ssrf_target` resolves non-literal hostnames, so without this
    every hostname assertion below would depend on the resolver the suite
    happens to run against -- `ollama.internal` is a name a corporate split
    horizon really can answer with an RFC1918 address.

name: test_ollama_base_url_validation
docstring: S-15: _ollama_base validates scheme and rejects bad URLs.

name: test_ollama_base_allows_loopback_in_both_families
docstring:
`ollama serve` binds loopback by default, so loopback must never be blocked.

    `::1` is the regression this pins: it is `is_loopback` *and* `is_reserved`
    *and* `is_private`, so any guard that tests the block predicates before
    loopback rejects the documented IPv6 local address.

name: test_ollama_base_blocks_pivot_only_literals
docstring:
Addresses that are never an Ollama server and only ever a pivot target.

    `fd00:ec2::254`, `192.0.0.192` and `100.100.100.200` are the metadata
    endpoints that are *not* link-local (unique-local, private and CGNAT
    respectively), so they only get caught by being named.
    `::ffff:169.254.169.254` is here because the IPv4-mapped form inherits none
    of the v4 address's classifications -- it has to be unwrapped to be seen.

name: test_ollama_base_allows_lan_servers
docstring:
An Ollama server on the LAN is a normal deployment, not an SSRF target.

    Blocking RFC1918/ULA outright would break the main non-loopback use of
    OLLAMA_HOST to harden an operator-supplied env var against the operator.
    The plain-HTTP warning is the proportionate response and is asserted by
    `test_plain_http_ollama_off_loopback_warns`.

name: test_ollama_base_blocks_hostname_resolving_to_metadata
docstring:
A name whose A record points at the metadata endpoint must not pass.

    The pre-fix guard classified only literals and treated the `ValueError` on
    any hostname as "allowed", so this walked straight through.

name: test_ollama_base_blocks_hostname_with_one_bad_record
docstring:
Every resolved address is checked, not just the first.

    A split answer -- one routable address and one metadata endpoint -- would
    otherwise let the blocked target through on whichever record urlopen picks.

name: test_gemini_request_model_path_and_key_header
docstring: S-14/S-15: gemini request puts key in header and handles model path.

name: test_writer_falls_back_to_utf8_on_an_unknown_stream_encoding
docstring:
An unknown codec must not abort the answer, and must still emit the text.

    `_writer` catches LookupError and re-encodes through utf8. This asserted
    only that the call did not raise, so a fallback that silently dropped the
    chunk would have passed.

name: test_stream_answer_empty_or_error_body
docstring: S-15: stream_answer raises SystemExit with provider error details.

name: test_rag_target_resolution_github_spec
docstring: Item 6 (S-7): GitHub spec target is parsed and indexed via fetch.index_github.

name: test_rag_mistyped_local_path_never_clones
docstring:
#452 N1: `src/app` is also a valid owner/repo spelling, so a typo in a
    local path used to become a clone from github.com with the user's token.

name: test_rag_cli_answer_integration
docstring: Item 6 (S-7): `rag --answer` forwards provider and model to stream_answer.

name: test_rag_answer_exits_3_when_a_bound_cut_the_answer_short
docstring: #285: a partial answer is printed, but the exit status says it is partial.

name: test_score_rrf_with_precomputed_vectors
docstring: Item 7 (S-9): score_rrf with precomputed vectors dict ranks high-similarity chunks higher.

name: test_compress_pinned_literal_output
docstring: Item 8 (N-1 / N-2): _compress output has pinned literal headers/signature and no body.

name: test_expand_non_numeric_confidence_handled_defensively
docstring: S-8: non-numeric or None confidence does not raise and is treated as 0.0.

name: test_pack_context_disarms_citation_forgery
docstring: N-3: fake citation lines in chunk text are escaped with backslash in pack_context.

name: test_rag_provider_selection_and_missing_env
docstring: S-6: provider selection honours explicit flag and validates required env var.

name: test_pack_context_exclude_secrets_on_a_built_index
docstring:
S-6: pack_context(exclude_secrets=True) excludes secret paths from chunks and markdown.

    The no-vectors counterpart is
    `test_repo2graph.py::test_pack_context_exclude_secrets_without_vectors`: the
    exclusion has to hold on both the fused and the plain BM25 path, and the two
    reach `pack_context` through different scoring code.

name: test_configurable_secret_denylist
docstring: Issue 83: pack_context supports user-configurable secret keywords and directories.

name: test_cli_flags
docstring: Issue 83: CLI supports --secret-keyword, --secret-dir, and --exclude-secrets flags.

name: test_stream_answer_propagates_writer_broken_pipe
docstring: N-11: BrokenPipeError from stream writer propagates directly, not wrapped in SystemExit.

name: test_optional_rag_extra_and_untouched_core_dependencies
docstring: Verify the rag extra exists; core deps stay tree-sitter only.

name: test_how_to_read_documents_the_graphrag_protocol
docstring:
Verify HOW_TO_READ mentions pack_context + confidence filtering, and a
    freshly built manifest carries it.

name: test_no_splitlines_in_new_code
docstring: Verify splitlines() desyncs rows from tree-sitter .

name: test_emit_survives_every_stdout_error_handler
docstring:
_emit() must not raise whatever error handler stdout carries.

    Git Bash on Windows hands a piped stdout errors='surrogateescape', which
    still raises on a character the codec lacks -- so treating any non-strict
    handler as safe to print through crashed `repo2graph query ... > out.txt`
    on any repo holding, say, U+2192. cp1252 is pinned here because it is the
    encoding that actually ships the bug; U+2192 has no cp1252 mapping while
    U+2014 does, so the arrow is the character that proves it.

name: test_cli_version_and_bare
docstring: CLI QoL: --version and bare invocation behaviour.

name: test_pick_provider_google_api_key_fallback
docstring: answer.py: GOOGLE_API_KEY fallback and GEMINI_API_KEY precedence.

name: test_default_models_current_and_overridable
docstring: #130: DEFAULT_MODELS stay on current cheap/fast ids; --model overrides.

name: test_ollama_request_num_ctx_and_gemini_traversal
docstring: answer.py: Ollama sets num_ctx; Gemini blocks path traversal.

name: test_is_secret_path_expanded
docstring: query.py: _is_secret_path catches common credential patterns and directory segments.

name: test_is_secret_path_catches_dotless_env_kubeconfig_and_backups
docstring:
Three families that reached `chunks.jsonl` in the clear.

    Each of these is indistinguishable in content from a path the filter already
    excluded, so an agent calling `repo_search` -- or `rag --answer`, which POSTs
    the pack to a third-party provider -- got the credential verbatim.

name: test_the_backup_suffix_strip_terminates_on_a_hostile_name
docstring:
A path is attacker-supplied on every build, and this rule loops.

    Each pass removes at least one character and the loop stops when no suffix
    matches or nothing but the suffix is left, so a name that is nothing but
    thousands of stacked suffixes must return rather than recurse without bound.
    The time bound is deliberately loose (measured ~6ms for the worst of these).

name: test_is_secret_path_163_no_overmatch
docstring:
Verify _is_secret_path() must not over-match legitimate source files
    via bare substrings ("-env" in name, "token" in name), while still
    excluding genuinely secret-ish paths. Both directions pinned literally
    per CONTRIBUTING.md ("Tests must pin values, not compare the implementation to
    itself"). Verified as a detector: on the pre-fix code this test fails on
    the "must NOT match" assertions for react-app-env.d.ts and tokenizer.json.

name: test_expand_prevents_edge_starvation
docstring: query.py: expand() filters matching edges before capping candidates.

name: test_cli_corrupt_index_friendly_error
docstring: cli.py: corrupted index files yield a friendly error message instead of traceback.

name: test_cite_block_handles_none_line_numbers
docstring: query.py: _cite_block cleanly defaults missing/None start/end lines.

name: test_multi_segment_secret_dir_matching
docstring: Multi-segment extra_dirs like 'configs/secrets' must match paths under that prefix.

name: test_empty_secret_keyword_does_not_match_all
docstring: An empty string keyword must not match every file in the repository.

name: test_compressed_file_neighbour_cites_only_the_lines_it_shows
docstring: `[cite: JsonReader.kt:1-648]` sat over a header plus `/*`.

name: test_unmappable_compressed_neighbour_is_marked_not_overclaimed
docstring: A file residual's first shown line cannot be mapped back to a line.

name: test_pick_provider_refuses_to_guess_between_two_providers
docstring:
#452 N3: the destination of the user's source must be chosen, not inferred
    from whichever credentials happen to be exported.

name: test_query_inflection_finds_the_base_identifier
docstring:
#382: `validates`/`validation` did not match a symbol named `validate`.
    Stems are added beside the original term, query side only.

name: test_anthropic_thinking_field_only_for_models_that_accept_it
docstring:
#55: `thinking: disabled` is a 400 on models where thinking is always on,
    so only the listed defaults get it; an override is sent unchanged.

name: test_answer_refuses_a_pack_with_no_room_for_the_reply
docstring: #290: the prompt estimate plus MAX_TOKENS must fit the model's context.

name: _cochange_index
docstring: Two files that never reference each other but always change together.

name: test_expansion_presets_choose_which_edges_are_walked
docstring:
#289: CO_CHANGE is never walked by default, and a preset (or --edge-type)
    can opt into it; `why` names the edge that admitted each neighbour.

name: embedded_index
docstring: A mini index with real vectors on disk, built through the CLI.

name: test_cmd_rag_hands_score_rrf_a_real_vectors_argument
docstring:
The regression test for the original silent failure.

    `cmd_rag --vectors` must reach `score_rrf` with a non-None `vectors=`. The
    pre-v1.4.0 bug was precisely that it did not, while every surface around it
    reported success.

name: test_embed_writes_npy_and_meta_to_disk
docstring: A rag-enabled build leaves real .npy bytes behind, not just a report.

name: test_index_reads_the_npy_back
docstring: The vectors a later process loads are the ones that were written.

name: test_dense_ranking_differs_from_bm25_only
docstring:
Fusion must actually change the ranking, or it is not doing anything.

    A rigged embedder puts the BM25 *last* candidate nearest the query. If the
    vectors reach the ranker the fused order differs from the lexical one; if
    they are dropped on the way, the two are identical -- which is exactly what
    the pre-v1.4.0 path produced.

name: test_no_vectors_means_plain_bm25
docstring: The zero-dependency floor is untouched: no vectors, no change.

name: test_fusion_that_turns_itself_off_emits_a_structured_warning
docstring:
The silent degrade BACKLOG item 2 describes must now announce itself.

    `fuse_ok` passes -- model and width agree -- and fusion still abandons
    itself inside `_vectors_for` because one shortlisted chunk has no vector.
    That used to be silent, which meant a lexical answer to a question the
    caller explicitly asked to be answered densely.

name: test_successful_fusion_records_full_coverage
docstring: The happy path sets coverage and says nothing on stderr.

name: test_verify_rag_reports_a_healthy_index
docstring: --verify-rag exits 0 and names the model and dimension.

name: test_verify_rag_fails_when_the_index_has_no_vectors
docstring: No vectors is a non-zero exit with an actionable message.

name: test_verify_rag_fails_on_a_model_mismatch
docstring: A different active embedder is a refusal naming both sides.

name: test_verify_rag_fails_on_a_dimension_mismatch
docstring: Same model id, different width: still a refusal, never a best effort.

name: test_verify_rag_reports_partial_chunk_coverage
docstring: The failure fuse_ok cannot see: some chunks have no vector at all.

name: test_verify_rag_never_defaults_the_model_to_the_index_claim
docstring:
The guard must compare against the *configured* model, not the index's.

    Defaulting the query-side model id to `vector_meta["model_id"]` makes
    fuse_ok compare a value with itself: permanently true, and the guard is
    gone. This asserts the default that reaches `default_embedder` is the
    built-in one, never the index's claim.

name: test_the_default_rag_path_opens_no_socket
docstring: A plain `rag` must not touch the network, with or without vectors on disk.

name: test_double_star_spans_zero_directories
docstring: '**/*.py' must also pick up top-level files; Path.match does not.

name: test_discover_finds_non_ascii_filenames
docstring: git ls-files escapes such paths unless asked for NUL-separated output.

name: test_parse_bases_are_names_not_keywords
docstring: Grammars wrap supertypes in clauses; 'extends B' is not a usable name.

name: test_parse_multi_param_generic_bases
docstring:
Verify commas inside a generic's type args must not split the base list.

    `class Repo(Generic[T, U], BaseRepo)` used to split on every raw comma,
    yielding the malformed tokens ['Generic[T', 'U]', 'BaseRepo'] instead of
    the two real bases. Same bug for `<...>` template/generic args in
    TS/Java/C++.

name: test_parse_survives_deep_nesting
docstring: The walker must not recurse; deep trees used to raise RecursionError.

name: test_parse_lua_extracts_functions_and_calls
docstring: Verify Lua function definitions, docstrings, and calls extraction.

name: test_build_lua_calls_edge
docstring: Verify build indexes .lua files and creates CALLS edges.

name: test_import_targets_relative_bare_dot
docstring:
`from . import X` / `from .. import X, Y`: the dots have no module name of
    their own, so the imported names ARE the submodule targets (#160). Before the
    fix, import_targets() returned ["."]/[".."] and dropped the names entirely.

name: test_import_targets_python_from_import_captures_symbol
docstring: Verify `from pkg import name` must carry `name`, not just `pkg`.

name: test_resolve_import_prefers_submodule_file_over_init
docstring: Verify `mypkg/mymod.py` exists, so `from mypkg import mymod` must resolve to it.

name: test_resolve_import_falls_back_to_init_when_no_submodule_file
docstring: Verify no `mypkg/thing.py` on disk -- `thing` must be a name in __init__.py.

name: test_resolve_import_keeps_dot_directories
docstring: A leading '.' in a real directory name must not be stripped.

name: test_build_edges_bare_dot_relative_import
docstring:
`from . import utils` must register an IMPORTS edge to the sibling module
    pkg/utils.py, not to pkg/__init__.py (#160).

name: test_split_breaks_a_line_longer_than_max_chars
docstring:
Hand-built fixture pinning literal chunk boundaries (CONTRIBUTING.md: assert
    literal values, not a property the old, buggy code also happened to hold).

    text = "AAAAAAAAAA\nBB\n" (a 10-char line the packer alone can't shrink,
    plus a short second line), max_chars=5. Before the fix, _split returned a
    single 14-char chunk (the whole first line plus every line the packer
    could still fit) because the inner loop always appended at least the
    first line regardless of its own length -- an unbounded chunk.

name: test_iter_chunks_streams_without_materialising
docstring:
iter_chunks is a generator (chunk text is the biggest allocation on a big
    repo); build_chunks stays a list for API stability.

name: test_file_chunk0_id_matches_node_id
docstring:
Verify file chunk 0 uses the unsuffixed node id, same as symbols.

    On main, file chunks were `file:{path}#0` while symbol chunk 0 was
    `sym:{path}::{qualname}`. A lookup for `file:notes.md` therefore missed
    chunk 0 unless the caller stripped `#0`. Multi-part splits still get
    `#1`, `#2`, … so ids stay unique and ordered.

name: test_index_survives_unicode_line_separators
docstring:
U+2028 is a line break for splitlines() but not for JSON; it must not
    split a chunk record in half.

name: test_query_on_a_partial_index_exits_cleanly
docstring:
A build that excludes the jsonl format still writes chunks.jsonl but no
    nodes/edges. Querying that used to raise FileNotFoundError out of Index,
    because the pre-flight check only looked at chunks.jsonl.

name: test_manifest_usage_hints_are_present_and_non_empty
docstring:
usage_hints lets an agent orient without a round-trip tool call: every
    key is populated, and edge_type_meanings/what_is_not_indexed are derived
    from the same source manifest.json's top-level edge_types and the skip
    labels write_overview_human's "What was skipped" section uses -- not a
    second hand-authored copy that can drift.

name: test_manifest_states_the_fan_out_this_build_used
docstring:
#245: the fan-out limit is per build (`--max-call-candidates`), but the
    manifest's prose used to hardcode "up to 5" -- so an index built with 2
    shipped an artifact asserting 5, to an agent that was told the manifest is
    authoritative. Both limits here are non-default literals on purpose: at the
    default the buggy text and the correct text are the same string, so a test
    run only at 5 detects nothing.

name: test_manifest_defaults_when_the_graph_never_went_through_build
docstring:
write_manifest has only ever duck-typed `g`, and a Graph assembled by
    hand has no build to inherit a fan-out limit from. It must still write a
    manifest stating the default rather than raising: a wrong number is the
    #245 bug, but no manifest at all is worse than one carrying the default.

name: BareGraph
signature: class BareGraph:  # only what write_manifest has ever required of `g`

name: test_chunk_neighbours_carry_structured_edge_info
docstring:
caller_edges/callee_edges/base_edges are the additive, structured
    sibling of callers/callees/bases: same targets, plus edge_type,
    edge_direction and -- only when ambiguous -- confidence.

name: test_graphml_preserves_custom_nodegraphics_edgegraphics_attributes
docstring: Verify write_graphml preserves custom attributes named nodegraphics and edgegraphics.

name: test_overview_lists_hubs
docstring: human/overview.md gets the new structured map (artifact_path resolves human/).

name: test_embed_flips_has_vectors_in_stats_json
docstring:
has_vectors is read from the same has-vectors-been-written fact
    register_written already appends vectors.npy for -- not a hardcoded
    guess, and not re-derived independently.

name: test_write_overview_human_at_a_glance_matches_graph_stats
docstring: New human/overview.md: structured sections whose numbers come from g.stats.

name: test_agent_overview_keeps_the_old_prose_format
docstring: agent/overview.md must stay byte-for-byte what write_overview() produces today.

name: test_graph_shape_matches_the_characterization
docstring: Node ids, (src, dst, type) triples and chunk ids match the pinned literals.

name: test_symbol_chunk_body_survives_unicode_line_separator
docstring:
Verify a file whose first line holds U+2028 must still slice each
    later symbol's chunk from the right source lines. Currently, `splitlines()`
    splits on U+2028 while tree-sitter row numbers do not, so the body comes out
    as "\\ndef uses_sep():" and never contains "return MSG".

name: test_file_residual_excludes_symbol_body
docstring:
Verify the residual chunk holds only lines no symbol claimed. At
    HEAD the same mis-slice pulls `return MSG` (the body of uses_sep) into the
    residual and drops part of the real residual span.

name: test_cochange_survives_non_ascii_filenames
docstring:
Verify two non-ASCII paths committed together three times
    must yield a CO_CHANGE edge. Currently, `git log` runs with text=True and
    core.quotepath=true, so the paths come back quoted/locale-decoded, never
    match file_index, and the edge silently vanishes (or raises
    UnicodeDecodeError on a non-UTF-8 locale).

name: FakeGitProc
docstring:
Stand-in for the `git log` child `add_cochange` streams .

    add_cochange no longer calls run(capture_output=True), which handed back a
    CompletedProcess with the whole blob attached; it opens a Popen and reads
    the pipe in blocks, stopping at MAX_COCHANGE_BYTES. A fake therefore has to
    behave like a process -- a readable stdout, plus the kill/poll/wait trio the
    reaping path uses.

name: fake_git_popen
signature: def fake_git_popen(stdout: bytes, returncode: int = 0, seen=None):
docstring: A Popen replacement that always yields `stdout`, recording the argv.

name: test_add_cochange_splits_git_log_on_newline_only
docstring:
Verify add_cochange must split
    `git log` output on "\\n" only. With core.quotepath=false git emits a path
    containing a raw U+2028; str.splitlines() would cut that path in two so
    neither fragment matches file_index and the CO_CHANGE edge vanishes.

name: test_graphml_roundtrips_with_a_control_char
docstring:
Verify a C0 control char inside a docstring must not make the
    GraphML unparseable. stdlib only, never skipped. Currently, ElementTree writes
    the raw \\x0c and ET.parse raises ParseError.

name: test_parse_spec_rejects_traversal_and_option_specs
docstring:
Verify traversal / option-like specs must raise. Currently,
    parse_spec("owner/..") returns ("owner", "..") instead of raising.

name: test_parse_spec_still_accepts_valid_specs
docstring: Verify the hardening must not reject legitimate specs.

name: _RunRecorder
docstring: Stand-in for subprocess.run that records every call and reports success.

name: test_token_never_appears_in_clone_argv
docstring:
Verify no argv element handed to subprocess.run may contain the
    token. Currently the token is interpolated into the clone URL argv element.

name: test_every_fetch_subprocess_call_passes_timeout
docstring:
Verify every subprocess.run in fetch.py must carry a timeout
    and specify encoding='utf8' and errors='replace'.

name: test_discover_matches_between_git_and_walk
docstring:
Verify discover() must return the same relative paths whether or
    not the tree is a git checkout. Currently the os.walk fallback drops every
    dot-directory while the git path keeps it, so `.github/**` appears only in a
    git checkout.

name: test_parse_all_falls_back_when_the_pool_breaks
docstring:
Verify a BrokenProcessPool must fall back to the serial path and
    return the jobs=1 result for all files without raising.

name: test_build_takes_the_pool_path_above_parallel_min_files
docstring:
#67: every other fixture is under PARALLEL_MIN_FILES, so nothing in the
    suite ever entered `parse_all`'s ProcessPoolExecutor branch -- which is how
    the MCP auto-build hang (#90) survived a green run.

    `wide_repo` crosses the threshold, and this asserts the branch is taken
    *and* that the pool is built with the initializer that keeps its workers
    off whatever stdin/stdout the parent had.

name: test_dead_dataclass_fields_are_gone
docstring:
Verify Symbol has no start_byte/end_byte and ParsedFile
    has no file_calls. Currently, all three fields are present.

name: _run_blocks
docstring: Yield the body of every `run: |` / `run: >` block-scalar in a workflow.

name: test_index_repo_workflow_has_no_run_interpolation
docstring:
Verify no `${{ inputs. }}` or `${{ github.event. }}` inside any
    run: block of index-repo.yml; the slug is computed from "$R2G_REPO". Currently,
    the "Compute slug" step interpolates ${{ inputs.repo }} straight into bash.

name: test_ci_workflow_tests_job_covers_windows
docstring:
Verify the ci.yml `tests` job runs on ubuntu and windows across
    both Python versions. Currently the matrix is ubuntu-latest only.

name: _top_block
docstring: The body of a top-level `key:` mapping, as text.

name: _declared
docstring: Names declared directly under a top-level mapping (inputs:/outputs:).

name: _defaults
docstring: {input name: default string} for action.yml's inputs: block.

name: _step
docstring: The YAML chunk of the composite step carrying `id: <step_id>`.

name: _argv
docstring: (subcommands, options) the repo2graph CLI is invoked with in one step.

name: _uses_local_with
docstring: Keys passed via `with:` to every `uses: ./` step in a workflow.

name: test_action_yml_run_blocks_take_inputs_only_through_env
docstring:
Every composite `run:` script reads its inputs from env:, never from a
    ${{ }} expression -- an input holding shell metacharacters would otherwise
    be substituted into the script before bash ever sees it.

name: test_action_yml_cli_subcommands_and_flags_exist
docstring:
Every subcommand and option action.yml hardcodes into its argv is a real
    repo2graph CLI surface. Rename a CLI flag and this fails.

name: test_action_yml_summary_keys_are_emitted_by_build

    the byte-budget tests below derive their budgets from exactly that length.

name: test_max_edges_truncation_is_deterministic
docstring:
Two builds of one tree under one ceiling keep the *same* edges.

    This is the property that makes a bounded index usable at all. Discovery is
    sorted, so edges are added in a fixed order and the prefix the ceiling keeps
    is fixed too. If that ever stopped holding, two machines would hold
    different subsets of the same graph and each would answer questions the
    other could not -- the same failure `--max-files` had before discovery was
    sorted.

name: test_a_dropped_duplicate_is_not_counted_against_the_ceiling
docstring:
`add_edge` dedupes before it checks the limit.

    Counting a repeat as a drop would make `edges_dropped` report loss that did
    not happen, and would let a graph with many duplicate edges trip a ceiling
    it never actually reached.

name: test_a_duplicate_of_a_dropped_edge_is_also_counted_once
docstring:
`edges_dropped` counts distinct edges lost, not attempts.

    The sibling test above covers a repeat of an edge that *was* added -- the
    dedupe check sees it and returns before the ceiling. A repeat of an edge the
    ceiling already rejected took the other path: `_edge_seen.add(key)` sat after
    the ceiling's `return`, so the key was never recorded and every re-proposal
    was counted again. `edges_dropped` is published in stats.json and read as the
    number of edges the graph is missing, so counting attempts overstated the
    loss for any edge discovered more than once -- which is

name: test_max_bytes_stops_at_a_prefix_of_discovery_order
docstring:
The budget keeps a prefix, never a best-fit selection.

    Skipping an oversized file and continuing would make which small files are
    indexed depend on the sizes of files *after* them, so adding one large file
    in the middle of a repository could silently change the tail of the
    selection. A prefix is the only reproducible answer.

    `CALLS_EXTERNAL` edge (`ambiguous`) or an `external` node -- 8 of the fields
    this module declares. A drift detector blind to a third of the surface is the
    kind of test that passes while the contract rots, so this builds a repo that
    does emit them rather than asserting against the same narrow fixture twice.

name: test_self_recursive_call_resolves_to_itself
docstring:
A top-level function calling its own name recurses; it does not bind elsewhere.

    Every tier filtered the calling symbol out with `c != sid`, so `helper`'s
    recursive call was handed to the same-named *method* at confidence 1.0 and
    the recursion edge disappeared: one edge, confidently wrong.

name: test_unambiguous_method_recursion_keeps_its_self_edge
docstring: A method whose name is unique in its file recurses onto itself, confidently.

name: test_a_methods_own_name_is_never_bound_confidently
docstring:
`c.to_dict()` inside `Report.to_dict` is never a self-call.

    The call has a receiver that is not self, so the caller is not a candidate
    (audit round 2: receiver-aware tier 0) and the sibling is the only reading.

    This is the shape of repo2graph's own doctor.py:61,
    `[c.to_dict() for c in self.checks]`, which an earlier version of this fix
    resolved to `Report.to_dict` itself and got confidently wrong.

name: test_method_recursion_survives_a_same_named_sibling
docstring:
Recursion is never dropped, even when the name is ambiguous in the file.

    The bug this guards: every tier excluded the caller with `c != sid`, so the
    self-edge could not be emitted at all and the call was handed wholesale to
    the sibling at confidence 1.0.

name: test_decorator_call_counted_once
docstring:
A Python decorator is one call, not two.

    `decorated_definition` and `prev_sibling` both matched the same decorator
    node -- in tree-sitter-python the function_definition's prev_sibling *is*
    the decorator -- so `count` came out 2 on every decorated def in the repo.

name: test_stacked_decorators_each_counted_once
docstring: Two decorators produce two edges of one call each, not two of two.

name: test_dynamic_call_kind_is_language_scoped
docstring:
`send` is an ordinary Python method name, not a dynamic invocation.

    The heuristic matched a flat name list against the bare callee, so
    `queue.send(msg)`, `channel.send(x)` and `fn.apply(...)` were all published
    as `call_kind='dynamic'` evidence in every language.

name: test_csharp_and_php_import_alias_fields
docstring:
C# writes `alias = target`; PHP writes `target as alias`. Both were inverted.

    `using Foo = Bar.Baz;` parsed to `module='Foo', alias='Bar'`, so a call to
    `Bar(...)` resolved at confidence 1.0 to a symbol named `Foo` while the real
    alias resolved to nothing.

name: test_long_named_import_still_yields_details
docstring:
Import details parse the full text, not the 300-char artifact cap.

    `imports` is capped for artifact size and `parse_import_details` consumed
    that capped string, so a barrel import lost its closing brace and its
    `from "./mod"` and produced zero details -- every binding invisible to
    tier-3 resolution, with nothing recording the loss.

name: test_inherits_edges_do_not_duplicate_their_own_dst
docstring: `resolved_target` was a verbatim copy of the edge's `dst`, in every export.

name: test_explain_path_reports_a_symlink_as_non_regular
docstring:
`explain-path` must answer for the link, not its target.

    It resolved the path before `lstat`, so a symlink stat'd as its regular-file
    target and was reported INCLUDED -- for a path `discover()` drops, because
    discovery lstats what it walks. Same class as commit 8ddd010.

name: test_cache_entry_round_trip_keeps_resolution_evidence
docstring:
A cache entry must carry every field call resolution reads back out of it.

    `import_details`, `call_details` and `base_details` were all missing from the
    serialised entry, so a cache hit reconstructed them empty: an aliased import
    became an external call, and every decorator call came back `static`.

name: test_a_cache_without_resolution_evidence_is_refused
docstring:
A cache written before this PR must be rejected, not half-read.

    Its entries carry no `import_details`, `call_details` or `base_details`, so
    every cached symbol would come back with `call_kind='static'` and every
    aliased import unresolved. `PARSE_CACHE_FORMAT` is the only thing standing
    between such a cache and a silently wrong incremental build, which is why
    the constant has to move whenever an entry's shape does.

name: test_strict_parse_error_is_not_retried_serially

    `parse_all`'s blanket `except Exception` caught it and re-parsed every file
    serially before raising the same error, doing the whole build's parse twice
    on the way to failing.

name: test_repeated_begin_without_end_stays_linear
docstring:
The detector for the quadratic form.

    At 200k characters the paired scan takes tens of milliseconds; the lazy
    single-pattern form took ~8 seconds, and ~8 minutes at the 1.5 MB file
    ceiling. The bound below sits far from both, so it survives a slow CI box
    without going vacuous.

name: test_repeated_incomplete_begin_header_stays_linear
docstring:
`PEM_BEGIN_RE` itself must not backtrack, which the test above cannot see.

    That one feeds *complete* `[REDACTED:private_key]` headers, which
    match on the first try with no backtracking -- it detects the `_pem_spans`
    pairing fix, not the anchor regex. The quadratic input is an *incomplete*
    header: `[-A-Z0-9_ ]` contains every character of `PRIVATE KEY`, so at each
    of the n/11 offsets where `-----BEGIN ` matches, the engine walks the whole
    remaining tail before failing. Measured on the unbounded `*` form: 1.10 s at
    107 KB, 17.6 s at 440 KB, ~90 s at 1 MB --

name: test_redact_content_on_repeated_begin_stays_linear
docstring:
redact_content runs the scan and then rewrites; both must stay bounded.

    Sized at 200k, not 100k: at 100k the quadratic form takes ~2s, which slips
    under this bound and makes the test a detector in name only. At 200k the
    fixed form takes ~0.8s and the quadratic one ~8s.

    CPU time, not wall clock, in all three tests here: under `-n auto` on a
    shared Windows runner, preemption alone pushed the fixed form to 13s.

name: test_a_future_dated_source_does_not_rebuild_the_cache

Freshness is the index's `build_id`, never an mtime comparison.

    The first version of this resolver compared the database's mtime with
    `nodes.jsonl`'s, which rebuilt on *every* query whenever a source file
    carried a future timestamp -- clock skew between a build host and a query
    host, or a restored archive -- because the newly written database was
    still "older" than its own input. A `build_id` is an identity rather than
    an ordering, so a clock cannot outrun it.

name: test_build_lock_falls_back_inside_an_unwritable_parent
docstring:
The documented read-only container run must be able to take the lock.

    `BuildLock` puts its file beside the target (`/out` -> `/.out.r2glock`) so
    it survives a swap of that directory. The documented container run mounts
    only `/out` writable with `/` read-only, so that sibling is unwritable and
    `repo2graph build -o /out` failed outright with "cannot create build lock
    /.out.r2glock: Read-only file system" -- a deployment `.github/SECURITY.md`
    describes in detail could not actually run. CI never caught it because the
    container job that exercises it is newer than the bu

name: test_build_lock_prefers_the_sibling_when_the_parent_is_writable
docstring: The fallback must not fire on an ordinary build, or the swap guarantee is lost.

name: test_an_unusable_cache_dir_is_diagnosed_not_a_traceback
docstring:
`REPO2GRAPH_CACHE_DIR` is operator-supplied, so it can be anything.

    Its `mkdir` sits outside the `OSError` handling that guards the primary
    path, so a file standing where the directory must go escaped as a raw
    `FileExistsError` -- `_open_index` catches `(KeyError, ValueError,
    FileNotFoundError, StoreUnusable)`, and that is none of them. Same defect as
    #501, reached through the env var instead.

name: test_a_cache_that_cannot_be_opened_rebuilds_instead_of_raising
docstring:
An `OSError` opening a cache must degrade, not escape.

    The fast path caught only `sqlite3.DatabaseError`, but opening the file can
    fail for reasons SQLite never sees: another process holding it open at the
    OS level on Windows, or permissions changed after it was written. Neither is
    in `_open_index`'s catch list, so it surfaced as a traceback. The right
    response is the one a corrupt file already gets -- rebuild.

    Simulated, because an OS-level lock SQLite does not translate is not
    something a test can portably create.

    must never be evicted; a caller polling an id that *was* evicted gets a
    clean None (the "unknown task" answer), not a crash.

name: RecordingLock
docstring:
A drop-in for threading.Lock (which rejects attribute assignment)
    that counts how many times it was actually held.

name: test_repo_build_status_is_never_cached
docstring: A cached progress report is the one answer guaranteed to be out of date.

name: test_a_failed_build_leaves_the_server_usable
docstring: Every later call gets a clear error; nothing crashes or retries forever.

name: test_an_existing_index_is_opened_directly
docstring: The task machinery must not get in the way when there is nothing to build.

name: test_async_build_is_off_by_default
docstring:
The synchronous build is a considered default, not an oversight.

    A build that outlives its client still writes a real index to disk, so the
    retry is instant -- a failure that heals itself. --async-build exists for
    the case that reasoning does not cover: a very large repo behind a client
    whose tool-call timeout no single build can fit inside.

name: test_default_estimator_runs_in_background_thread
docstring: Issue 151: TaskManager.start does not run _default_estimator synchronously on calling thread.

name: test_demotion_lowers_test_scores_and_leaves_source_alone
docstring:
The mechanism, asserted directly rather than through an emergent ranking.

    Whether source then *wins* a slot depends on how close the two were, which
    is a property of the corpus and belongs to the benchmark
    (`benchmarks/real/`), not to a fixture. A unit test tuned to sit in the
    narrow band where the penalty decides the order would be testing its own
    calibration: make the source slightly more on-topic and it passes without
    any fix at all, which is exactly what happened while writing this.

name: test_demotion_is_stable_for_equal_scores
docstring: Two candidates the penalty does not separate keep BM25's order.

name: test_a_test_shaped_question_is_not_demoted
docstring: The penalty must be off entirely when the question is about tests.

name: test_a_test_question_still_gets_the_tests
docstring: Demotion must not break the documented "what tests cover X" use case.

name: test_tests_remain_reachable_as_neighbours
docstring: The IMPORTS edge from a test back to the code under test must still work.

name: test_the_direction_survives_a_question_about_tests
docstring: The reason this is a separate predicate: both answers must be available.

name: test_a_caller_shaped_test_question_still_gets_the_tests
docstring: The defect, end to end: the penalty must not fire on this question.

name: test_a_question_mentioning_tests_keeps_source_for_a_non_test_question
docstring: The penalty must still fire for a question that is not about tests.

name: test_paged_repo_neighbours_lists_tests_and_honours_min_confidence
docstring: A cursor pages the same answer: TESTS rows included, the same floor applied.

name: run_embed
docstring: `repo2graph embed` -> the JSON report it printed.

name: sim_vector
docstring: A 2-D unit vector whose cosine against [1.0, 0.0] is exactly `sim`.

name: rigged_order
docstring:
The dense ranking this suite rigs: BM25 rank 2 first, rank 1 third.

    Swapping only ranks 1 and 2 is not enough -- reciprocal rank fusion gives
    the two chunks identical fused scores and the outcome turns on a tie-break.
    Demoting the BM25 winner to dense rank 3 makes the intended chunk win
    outright, whatever the tie-break rule is.

name: rigged_sims
docstring: {chunk index: vector} giving `rigged_order` against the query vector.

name: test_text_hashes_track_the_chunk_text

name: test_write_then_load_round_trips_exactly

name: test_meta_is_a_sibling_json_file

name: test_embed_appends_to_the_manifest_without_disturbing_it

Verify the two artifacts appear in `written` and `files`; every other

name: test_index_loads_vectors_keyed_by_chunk_list_index

name: test_index_without_vectors_reports_none

name: test_corrupt_vectors_degrade_silently

Verify a bad pair leaves idx.vectors None, raises nothing, and

name: test_vectors_for_unknown_chunk_ids_are_dropped

name: rewrite_meta

name: test_write_vectors_stamps_the_literal_format_marker
docstring: Verify value on disk is the one this suite checks against.

name: test_load_vectors_accepts_a_correctly_stamped_pair
docstring:
Verify neutrality: the valid format marker loads cleanly, or the gate is
    just 'vectors are off'.

name: test_load_vectors_refuses_an_unrecognised_format
docstring:

    -- is a ValueError, the same shape as the chunk_ids and row-count checks.

name: test_a_bad_format_degrades_to_bm25_end_to_end
docstring:
Verify through query.Index, a format bump is indistinguishable
    from having no vectors -- nothing raises, and the pack still answers.

    The correctly-stamped load is asserted first so this cannot pass by
    fusion being dead in the fixture for some unrelated reason.

name: test_model_id_of_reads_the_embedder
docstring: Verify the identity fuse_ok compares comes off the embedder.

name: test_fuse_ok_rejects_a_model_mismatch
docstring: Verify (False, reason) naming the index model and the query model.

name: test_fuse_ok_rejects_a_dim_mismatch
docstring:
Verify same model id, different width, still refused -- and the
    reason names both widths.

name: test_fuse_ok_accepts_a_match
docstring: Verify the matching case is accepted, or the guard is just 'off'.

name: mismatched_index
docstring: An index embedded with `stub/alpha`, with `stub/beta` now active.

name: test_rag_vectors_on_a_mismatch_exits_and_emits_no_pack
docstring:
Verify explicit --vectors fails loudly, names both model ids, and does
    not print a pack.

name: test_rag_without_a_vector_flag_degrades_to_bm25
docstring:
Verify auto mode exits 0, emits a pack, and does not fuse -- proved by
    the pack being identical to the same query with vectors switched off.

name: test_no_vectors_equals_an_index_with_the_files_deleted
docstring:
Verify `rag --no-vectors` against a *matching* vectorised index gives
    exactly what the same command gives once the two files are removed.

name: test_no_vectors_matches_the_baseline_golden
docstring: Verify --no-vectors is the baseline BM25 pack, byte for byte.

name: test_a_rigged_dense_ranking_changes_the_top_chunk
docstring:
Verify via the in-memory `vectors=` contract Index will populate.

    The dense ranking is supplied by the test, so the only thing asserted is
    which chunk *id* comes first -- no score, no rank number, no float.

name: test_a_rigged_embedder_changes_the_top_chunk
docstring:
Verify the same through the `embedder=` path, with a scripted
    embedder that never looks at the text it is handed.

name: test_mismatched_vector_dims_degrade_to_bm25
docstring:
Verify a candidate vector whose width does not match the
    query vector's must not silently truncate through zip() and produce a
    meaningless cosine score. It must disable fusion and fall back to BM25,
    handled as an invalid vector without raising unhandled exceptions out of
    score_rrf, and never fuse a truncated, meaningless similarity in.

name: test_rag_vectors_uses_the_persisted_vectors
docstring:
Verify `rag --vectors` on a matching index succeeds and consults the
    embedder (so the flag is wired through, not silently a no-op).

name: test_second_embed_reuses_everything
docstring: Verify reused == vectors, embedded == 0, and vectors.npy is byte-identical.

name: test_only_changed_chunks_are_re_embedded
docstring:
Verify embedded >= 1, reused >= 1, and `encode` saw only the texts of
    the chunks whose text actually changed.

name: test_force_disables_reuse
docstring: Verify `embed --force` after a successful embed reports reused == 0.

name: test_embed_reports_model_and_dim
docstring:
Verify the report carries every key the reuse criteria
    read, so a partial implementation fails here rather than with a KeyError.

name: test_rag_embed_model_reaches_the_query_embedder
docstring: R-1: `rag --vectors --embed-model X` embeds the query with X.

name: test_query_embed_model_reaches_the_query_embedder
docstring: R-1 (b): the same on `query`, which shares the helper but not the test.

name: test_without_embed_model_a_custom_model_index_is_refused
docstring:
R-2: the flag is load-bearing, not cosmetic -- omit it against an index
    embedded with a non-default model and the guard fires, naming both.

name: test_rag_model_stays_the_llm_model
docstring:
R-3: `--model` and `--embed-model` are two dests, not one. The LLM name
    must never be handed to default_embedder, nor the checkpoint to the LLM.

name: test_the_default_path_builds_no_embedder
docstring:
R-4: dense fusion is opt-in, so neither `rag` nor `query` constructs an
    embedder without the flag -- constructing one downloads ~90 MB on a cold
    cache, and the default path promises no network.

name: test_explicit_vectors_still_builds_one
docstring: R-4 (b): the guard above must not pass by fusion being dead everywhere.

name: test_real_sentence_transformers_smoke_test
docstring: Smoke test against the real sentence-transformers wrapper.

name: test_read_bounded_does_not_allocate_its_limit
docstring:
A small file under a 512 MB ceiling must not cost a 512 MB buffer: on
    Windows that is real commit charge, and parallel test workers ran the runner
    out of memory with it.

name: test_an_oversized_vectors_npy_is_refused_before_it_is_read
docstring: The ceiling must bind before the bytes are materialised.

name: test_an_oversized_vectors_meta_is_refused
docstring:
The sidecar is read *before* the array, so it needs its own ceiling.

    A limit on vectors.npy alone would leave the whole allocation reachable
    through this file instead.

name: test_a_normal_vectors_pair_still_round_trips_under_the_real_limits
docstring: The guard must reject oversized files only -- not every file.

name: test_zero_width_rows_are_rejected_before_the_row_loop
docstring:
#474: with cols == 0 the payload-size check needs zero bytes, so a
    128-byte header claiming a trillion rows would pass it and spin the loop.

name: test_a_dropped_vector_set_says_why
docstring:
#456 P1: an oversized or corrupt vectors.npy used to vanish silently and
    ranking fell back to BM25 with nothing reporting it.

name: test_every_surface_matches_something_in_every_file_it_claims
docstring:
A pattern that matches nothing is a check that has become a no-op, which
    is exactly how the documented `@v1` survived the 2.0.0 release. `findings`
    reports that as a `<no match>` sentinel rather than silently passing.

name: test_the_repo_is_currently_consistent
docstring:
check_version.py is a required CI step; this is the same assertion at
    unit level so a failure names the surface rather than a subprocess exit.

name: test_release_commit_paths_cover_every_bumped_path_plus_the_changelog
docstring:
publish.yml passes this list to `--files`. A path `rewrite()` touches but
    the list omits produces a release commit that bumps some surfaces and not
    others, on a tag PyPI will not let you reuse.

name: test_files_mode_prints_exactly_those_paths
docstring:
The `--files` CLI is what publish.yml shells out to; if its output stops
    being a plain space-separated list, `read -ra` silently builds the wrong
    array.

name: test_every_surface_path_exists
docstring:
A renamed doc silently drops its surface from both the bump and the
    check, so the table naming a file that is gone must fail loudly.

name: test_precommit_hook_fires_for_every_surface_it_guards
docstring:
The `version-consistency` hook's `files:` regex must match every path in
    the surface table.

    The regex is maintained by hand next to a comment claiming it mirrors
    `version_surfaces.SURFACES`, and it had drifted both ways: it still named
    four deleted docs, and it had never been updated for `npm/package.json`,
    `CITATION.cff` or `docs/cli.md`, so a commit touching only those bumped a
    version the local hook never checked. CI runs `check_version.py`
    unconditionally, so this was a local-hook gap rather than a missed gate --
    which is exactly why nothing caught it.

name: test_bump_moves_every_surface_to_the_new_version
docstring: The whole point: after a bump, nothing still reads the old version.

name: test_bump_rewrites_the_documented_major_tag
docstring:
Named separately because it is the surface that was missed. `@v9` and
    "every 9.x release", hand-derived from a 9.9.9 target.

name: _rewrite_in_sandbox
signature: def _rewrite_in_sandbox(tmp_path: Path, version: str) -> dict[str, str]:
docstring:
Run `rewrite(version)` against copies, never the real checkout.

    `version_surfaces.ROOT` is module state, so it is swapped for the duration
    and restored -- a test that bumped the working tree and failed halfway would
    leave the repo claiming a version it never released.

name: test_the_sandbox_helper_leaves_the_real_tree_alone
docstring:
The guard on the guard: if `_rewrite_in_sandbox` ever edited the checkout,
    every other test here would still pass while corrupting the repo.

name: test_major_surfaces_carry_only_the_major
docstring:
`kind="major"` exists because publish.yml's floating tag is `vN`. If a
    major surface started expecting a full version, every bump would write
    `@v2.1.0` into a `uses:` line and point users at a tag that does not move.

name: test_every_changelog_heading_has_a_link_definition
docstring:
`## [3.0.0]` is a markdown reference link, so a heading without a
    matching `[3.0.0]: <url>` definition renders as the literal text `[3.0.0]`.

    The bug: `bump_changelog` wrote the heading and nothing wrote the
    definition, so every release from 1.5.1 on added a dead reference -- nine of
    them by 3.0.0 -- and `[Unreleased]` still diffed from v1.5.0. Nothing could
    fail on it, because no test read the foot of the file.

name: test_unreleased_diffs_from_the_newest_released_heading
docstring:
`[Unreleased]` must compare against the latest release, not whichever one
    happened to be current when the definition was last hand-edited.

name: test_bumping_the_changelog_adds_the_new_version_s_link_definition
docstring: The regression guard on the fix: heading and definition move together.

name: test_no_assertion_in_the_suite_spells_out_the_current_version
docstring:
A test that hardcodes the version under release is red the moment the
    bump lands -- and the first run that can see it is publish.yml's `pypi`
    job, which tests the already-tagged commit.

    The bug: tests/test_export_hardening.py asserted the static `__version__`
    fallback equalled `"2.2.0"`. Nothing could fail that until a bump rewrote
    the literal it was shadowing, so it passed every PR and aborted the 3.0.0
    release after the tag was cut and the bump PR merged. The fix is to read
    the surface -- `declared_version()` here, or the literal in
    `repo2graph/__init__.py` -

name: FakeGraph
docstring: The three attributes `write_html` reads off a Graph.

name: render
docstring: Write a page for a graph called `name` and hand back its HTML.

name: chrome
docstring: The two HTML contexts the repo name is interpolated into.

name: test_a_script_tag_in_the_repo_name_is_escaped
docstring: A repo literally named `<script>alert(1)</script>` must not execute.

name: test_attribute_and_tag_breakouts_in_the_repo_name_are_escaped
docstring: Neither the <title> nor the <h1> may be escaped out of.

name: test_the_data_placeholder_in_a_repo_name_is_not_expanded
docstring:
A repo named `__R2G_DATA__` must not pull the JSON payload into <h1>.

    The template is filled by a single regex pass over both placeholders, so a
    replacement's *output* is never rescanned. A naive sequence of `.replace`
    calls -- title first, then data -- would substitute the whole graph payload
    into the title and the heading.

name: test_the_payload_placeholder_still_receives_the_real_data
docstring: The single-pass guard must not break the substitution it protects.

name: test_angle_brackets_in_the_payload_cannot_close_the_script_block
docstring: `</script>` inside indexed content must not terminate the block early.

name: test_viz_nodes_zero_renders_no_nodes
docstring: 0 means an empty graph, not every node.

name: test_viz_nodes_none_is_the_no_cap_spelling
docstring: `all` on the CLI arrives here as None and keeps every node.

name: test_the_settle_loop_is_incremental_not_a_blocking_while
docstring:
Layout must yield to the browser between batches.

    A synchronous `while (alpha > ...) step()` blocks the main thread for the
    whole settle: no paint, no input, no scroll. Bounding the iteration count
    bounds the freeze but does not remove it.

name: test_the_iteration_cap_is_configurable_from_the_container
docstring: maxIterations defaults to 500 and is overridable per page.

name: test_a_progress_indicator_exists_and_is_hidden_when_idle
docstring: The user must be able to tell a laying-out page from a frozen one.

name: test_pointer_capture_is_released_on_both_pointerup_and_pointercancel
docstring:
A capture never released swallows every later pointer event on the page.

    This is a source-level assertion rather than a DOM test: a real one needs a
    JS runtime (jsdom or playwright), and this repo has no Node toolchain in its
    dev extra. It pins the property that actually regressed -- a handler losing
    its release call -- but it cannot prove the released id matches the captured
    one. This is the one untested-in-a-browser property here.

name: test_pointer_capture_release_is_guarded
docstring: releasePointerCapture throws if the element does not hold the capture.

name: test_the_page_is_self_contained
docstring: No network at render time and none at view time: one file, no fetches.

name: test_payload_is_valid_json
docstring: Whatever escaping is applied, the blob must still parse.

name: test_search_focus_and_legend_ui_are_present
docstring:
Presence check for the search box, focus mode and the legend panel.

    Not a browser test (this repo has no Node/jsdom toolchain in its dev
    extra, same limitation noted for the pointer-capture tests above) -- just
    confirms the three new pieces of UI actually landed in the rendered page
    and in TEMPLATE's script, rather than a full DOM/interaction check.

name: test_content_security_policy_is_present
docstring: graph.html must restrict resource loading and script execution via CSP.

name: test_a_node_fragment_seeds_the_page_without_becoming_markup
docstring:
#400: `graph.html#node=<id>` opens the detail view selected on that node.

    The VS Code extension's "Reveal in graph" opens the page this way. The
    fragment is whatever link the page was opened with, so it is treated like
    the repo name above: decoded defensively, bounded, compared by exact id,
    and only ever shown through text APIs. Source-level, for the reason the
    pointer-capture tests give.

name: test_generated_tables_match_the_core_ones
docstring: Adding a language, node type or edge type fails here until regenerated.

name: test_executables_cannot_be_set_by_a_workspace
docstring: A cloned repository's .vscode/settings.json must not choose what runs.

name: test_snapshot_watches_what_a_build_indexes_and_nothing_else
docstring:
The watched set is discovery's set, not an approximation of it (#483).

    This asserted `["src/a.py"]` while `discover` on the same tree yields
    `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `src/.a.py.swp` and `src/a.py~` as well -- a
    walk-fallback build indexes every file that is not in a skipped directory,
    whatever its name begins or ends with. Ignoring a file the build indexes is
    a rebuild that never happens, which is the whole failure `--watch` exists
    to avoid, so the dotfile and `~` rules are gone and the two sets agree.

name: test_snapshot_ignores_gitignored_paths
docstring:
A build never sees them, so a change to one must not trigger a rebuild.

    `snapshot` walked the tree itself, honouring no `.gitignore`: on
    repo2graph's own checkout that meant watching 305 files under
    `.hypothesis`, which every `pytest` run rewrites, so running the suite
    under `--watch` rebuilt continuously (#483).
